title: The send path records what it sent, in the same commit that can read it
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- api.request.send`s completion path writes the run. THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT
  OF THE TASK: nocx-rtg0 shipped an encrypted store, a key lifecycle, a
  budget, a retention policy, five settings controls and a query method whose
  WRITE path had no caller, and `deadcode is empty` could not see it, because
  RTA marks every method reached through an interface as reachable.
- The evidence is `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive <the record method> ./...`
  printing a path from main, contrasted against a method that is genuinely
  unwired. The contrast is what makes it evidence.
- A send that FAILS is recorded too — a run is what happened, not what
  succeeded.
- A stopped send records that it was stopped.
- The write failing does not fail the send: the person got their answer, and a
  store that could not keep it says so where the surface can render it, never
  only in a log.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, on feat/api-testing at 182d50e8, before that branch merges.

The store from nocx-kpl58.1 is on the branch and is NOT wired. deadcode cannot
report it — APIRunRepository is an interface, and RTA marks every method reached
through one as reflection-reachable — so the ratchet is green with the write path
dead. This is the ContentDB.Add shape AGENTS.md names.

The contrast, run as AGENTS.md prescribes:

  deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive '.../internal/content.sqliteContent.Ledger' ./...
    -> static@L1193 --> transport.NewWSServer
       ... --> capability.newAgentService
       dynamic@L0061 --> content.sqliteContent.Ledger          # WIRED

  deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive '.../internal/content.sqliteContent.Begin' ./...
    -> "reachable only through reflection"                     # NOT WIRED

Said a second way: grep for 'APIRuns()' outside internal/content finds five hits
and all five are test fakes returning nil.

So this task is the one that makes the feature exist, and until it lands nothing
a person does records a run. The PR body for #105 says so rather than implying
runs persist.

title: The store keeps one API exchange, under an identity that survives a restart
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A new typed repository on ContentDB beside Ledger() and Layout(), with its
  own tables and migration. NOT the ledger: consulted 2026-08-24, and the
  deciding fact is that the ledger`s `environments` model identifies an
  execution LOCATION (host, cwd, versioned observations pinned per execution)
  and cannot honestly say "collection X, request file Y, API environment Z".
- The identity a run is stored under is DURABLE. `ApiRun.handle` is minted per
  session and means nothing after a restart; the collection`s path and the
  request`s relPath are what a row carries.
- Request and response bodies go in artifacts + ordered chunks, never a large
  body column. `artifacts.execution_id` currently requires a LEDGER execution
  and LedgerRepository is declared that table`s sole writer — resolve that
  without creating two writers for one table, and say in the code which way
  and why.
- Retention: completed exchanges evict oldest-first under the existing budget,
  chunks cascading in the same transaction. A pending run is not a candidate.
- No credential is ever written. Asserted on the BYTES of the database, the
  way the vault`s tests already do it.
- Every external call has a test where it fails, and the partial failures are
  enumerated: what is true on disk when step 3 of 5 fails, and how the next
  start recovers.

title: A folder carries variables, and the requests inside it inherit them
description:
Owner's request of 2026-08-24, from the folder page: a folder should be able
to hold variables.

WHAT IT ADDS: a third scope in a chain that already has two. `substitute.go`
owns the order today — a request's own variables win over the environment's
plain values, and a request variable shadowing a name the environment
declares secret is REFUSED (ErrSecretShadowed, and the reason is written
there: a collection arriving in a pull request must not choose what a
reader's request sends). A folder's variables sit between those two, and
every rule that guards the request scope has to be answered again for this
one — including the shadowing refusal, which is the whole reason this is an
epic and not a field.

WHERE THEY LIVE: a file in the folder, listed by api.collections.list the
way `folders` already is, read and written by their own methods with their
own schema in contracts/. Bruno's `folder.bru` is the same shape one product
over. Not decided yet: the file's name and whether a folder file grows other
folder-level facts later (Postman puts auth and scripts there).

WHERE THEY ARE EDITED: the folder page (nocx-8aczn.8), which exists and is
the surface a person is already on when they are thinking about a folder.

## Success Criteria

- A person opens a folder, adds a variable, and a request inside that folder
  sends with it resolved — without an environment and without a variable of
  its own. One automated check watches exactly that, end to end.
- The order is asserted at every pair: a request's own variable wins over the
  folder's, and the folder's wins over the environment's plain value.
- A folder variable shadowing a name the environment declares SECRET is
  refused with the same sentence the request scope is refused with — the
  argument in substitute.go applies unchanged to a file in the same git
  repository.
- A folder with no variables file behaves exactly as it does today; nothing
  is written into a collection by opening it.
- The wire is a party: the folder file's shape is a JSON Schema in
  contracts/, the renderer's type is generated from it, and one test
  validates the real result off the real socket.

## Deliberately out

- Folder-level auth, scripts and tests (Postman has them; nothing has asked).
- Nesting rules beyond "the nearest folder up the path answers first".
close_reason:
All five children closed. A person can put a variable on a folder and every request inside it inherits it — request's own row, then nearest folder, then parents, then the environment's plain value, then the vault binding — and the Variables tab shows that whole chain with the winner marked and the loser rows named. The happy path is watched end to end by e2e/api-folder-variable.spec.ts, green in the container.

Six commits: 247fa5a8 (disk + resolution + variableFolders on four schemas), 50038587 (folder page edits them), 65b4f94b (api.request.scope + the tab + the address bar), a9192097 (e2e), 94722016 (the OS-split gate this exposed).

Two defects were caught in review that would otherwise have shipped: a suppression that would have made a refused delete silent while the folder page was open, and a second implementation of precedence in the renderer that was blind to the secret-shadowing refusal for unsaved rows. Both are recorded on .2 and .3.

Out of scope and still open: nocx-6hyke (a request remembers which stand it goes to), which reuses this chain's shape for the environment binding.

title: A selection offers to be attached, and never attaches itself
description:
Design: .internal/specs/2026-08-21-attaching-context-to-a-question-design.md §'The gesture' 1 and 4, approved 2026-08-21. Re-confirmed by the owner 2026-08-24 from a screenshot where a double-click raised 'block · row 16'.

Today: terminal-content.ts:2878 listens on document selectionchange → raiseChipFromSelection (:4123-4144), which freezes any qualifying selection into a chip. The predicate is already written and correct — chipFromSelection (ask-entry.ts:57) returns the block and row span or null — so what changes is who calls it and when.

The button is the kit's Button (variant primary, size sm) inside a surface-owned fixed wrapper: the surface PLACES, the kit paints. Read frontend/src/ui/README.md. Its viewport clamp is the same geometry problem as the block ⋮ menu (nocx-vnirv.2) and the kit's ui/context-menu.tsx:100-118 — use one implementation, do not write a third.
acceptance_criteria:
- A selection inside a finished block's output raises NO chip. Copying output attaches nothing; typing a command and pressing Enter afterwards runs it in the shell, with the affordance on screen.
- While such a selection exists, one Attach button floats near the end of it: never covering the selection, anchored below the last client rect, flipped above when there is no room, clamped to the viewport, and following the scrollback while the selection is alive.
- It disappears when the selection collapses, when it stops satisfying chipFromSelection (two blocks, a running block, the editor), and once pressed.
- Pressing it raises exactly ONE chip — including for a drag across three rows, simulated as the three intermediate selections a real drag fires.
- Attaching a region already attached is a no-op, not a second chip.
- Attaching does not move the input target and does not touch the selection (nocx-4wtlh's rule, now asserted with the affordance on screen).
- Every chip in the product is minted by ONE function, attachRegion(blockEl, rowStart, rowEnd); a test names it as the single seam.

title: session.read and session.list: one tool reads what is in a session, addressed or live
description:
internal/agenttools/registry.go:136-180. readScreen: 'reach for this for a command that is still RUNNING… a command that has already finished has left it'. blocks.read: 'Read a window of one FINISHED command's output'. The model is asked to decide on a fact it does not have. Measured cost from the owner's session: one question produced readScreen → blocks.list → blocks.read.

Execution site is the work: blocks.read is Executes:InGo (the ledger), readScreen is Executes:InRenderer (the broker), because a live command's output lives in xterm — AD-6. Executes is a property of the Declaration ROW today, so a tool whose execution site depends on the block's state is a change to that model. Read internal/agenttools/registry.go:105-124 and .internal/specs/2026-08-16-agent-tools-design.md before designing it.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE OWNER — a full-screen program on the alternate buffer (vim, htop) owns the screen and is NOT a block, so it has no id to address. Either readScreen survives with its description narrowed to exactly that case, or we decide the case is out of scope. Do not guess.
acceptance_criteria:
- One tool takes a block id and returns a window of that block's output plus the block's STATE — running, or exited with its code. The model never chooses a tool by whether the command has finished.
- It works for a block that is still running (the output is in the renderer) and for one that has finished (the output is in the ledger), and the person cannot tell from the outside which path served it.
- AD-6 is not crossed: the backend does not sniff the byte stream, and the live half is answered by the renderer through the broker, exactly as readScreen is today.
- The tool descriptions in the registry no longer instruct the model to pick by finished-vs-running.
- For every external call the new path makes, there is a test where that call fails — including the renderer being gone mid-call.
- The design question in the notes is ANSWERED IN THE BEAD by the owner before implementation starts.
notes:
OWNER DECISION 2026-08-24, in two parts.

PART 1 — the word 'block' leaves the tool names, and readScreen disappears as a NAME rather than as a capability.

- session.list — what can be addressed in this session right now. Empty in an unstructured pane, which is an honest answer and not an error.
- session.read — with an id, that item; WITHOUT an id, what is on the screen now.

So a finished command's output, a running command's output, the alternate buffer of a full-screen program, and a pane that has no blocks at all are ONE tool, and the model never chooses by a fact it does not have (whether the command has finished). The optional id is the whole mechanism: readScreen turns out to be session.read with no argument.

PART 2 — the namespace is the RESOURCE KIND the call addresses, not the product.

Rejected: nocx.read / nocx.list. Every tool in the product is nocx's, so that prefix partitions nothing; the real distinction would move into the suffix (nocx.listTabs, nocx.connect) and the prefix becomes a junk drawer — the same defect readScreen has.

Chosen: the closed content.ResourceKind set already in internal/content/ledger.go:242-250 (environment, session, path, credential, destination, tool). It is the axis the grant is scoped along (Declaration.Resources, Declaration.ResourceArg) and the axis a refusal already names. So the tool's name and its authority say one word: the Agent policy page shows rows over resources, the model sees the same nouns, the refusal names the same thing. Tabs and ssh connections arrive as new ResourceKinds — which they must anyway, for the policy to scope them — and their tool names follow rather than being invented.

Known limit, stated rather than glossed: this does not cover the whole registry. git.status is named by domain and addresses a path. The rule governs the axis the model actually chooses along; it is not a universal law.

WHY THE FULL-SCREEN CASE FOLDS IN (checked in code): a full-screen program IS a block — vim is submitted as a command, its running block exists, and enterFullscreen (frontend/src/scrollback/controller.ts:513) changes only the LAYOUT, not the block. Reading a running block already routes to the renderer, which reads the alternate buffer's viewport (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:945-951).

CAVEAT THE ANSWER MUST STATE: the alternate buffer has no scrollback (frontend/src/scrollback/controller.ts:207). What comes back is the CURRENT SCREEN, not accumulated output, and the result must say so rather than let the model read it as a window into history.

THE UNSTRUCTURED PANE is the case the no-id form serves: a pane with no shell integration has no blocks at all. Every pane starts that way (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:2212 — 'a conventional terminal, no ownership') and a host where integration cannot be installed stays that way (epic nocx-pu4).

title: Stop is on the live turn, in the place a command's Stop already is

title: One owner for 'working, nothing written yet' — on a turn and on a command
description:

title: Inline code inside bold or emphasis renders as code
description: inlineHtml (frontend/src/ui/answer-markdown.ts:84-101) takes the first alternation match and escapes its whole contents as text. Measured: '**`.herdr`** (14G)' matches as ONE bold token, so the backticks print. The comment at :63-72 explains — correctly — why code must win the alternation; what is missing is the other direction, that the CONTENTS of a bold or emphasis span are markup and must go through the inline pass again.

- `**`repos`** (8.7G)` renders 'repos' as a .ui-md-code chip inside a .ui-md-strong, with no literal backtick anywhere.
- The reverse never happens: the contents of a code span are never re-scanned, so ```**not bold**``` inside backticks keeps its asterisks. A test holds both directions.
- Nesting is bounded and cannot recurse without end on adversarial input.
- Every byte still goes through escapeHtml; no new element carries an attribute the model can influence.

title: Every list marker sits inside the block — bullets and numbers alike
description:
Cause, measured on the owner's screenshot: styles/components/answer-markdown.css:45-48 builds the hanging indent from padding-left plus text-indent:-1.2em. text-indent is an INHERITED property and .ui-md-marker (:65-69) is display:inline-block — a block container — so the -1.2em applies AGAIN to the marker's own first line. The glyph moves a further 1.2em left, out of .cmd-children's padding, and is clipped by its border-left (style.css:923-925). Both markerHtml call sites are affected: the bullet (answer-markdown.ts:139) and the ordered number (:132).

The one-line patch is .ui-md-marker { text-indent: 0 }. Prefer rebuilding the hanging indent WITHOUT text-indent (the property inherits and will bite the next thing placed in a list row); if you keep text-indent, say in the CSS why, beside the reset.
acceptance_criteria:
- A rendered list item's marker is fully inside the block: no part of the glyph is left of .cmd-children's content box, at depth 0 and at depths 1-3, for a bullet and for an ordered number.
- The marker and its item text are adjacent — the gap between them is the marker column's width, not the block's padding.
- Wrapped continuation lines of a list item still align under the item's text, which is what the hanging indent was for.
- A test asserts the geometry, not the declaration: it must fail on the current CSS.
