title: A tool call accounts for itself: one block-reading tool, and every call says how it went
description:
Two findings from the owner on 2026-08-24, joined because both change what a tool call reports.

TWO TOOLS FOR ONE QUESTION. internal/agenttools/registry.go:136-180 declares readScreen ('reach for this for a command that is still RUNNING … a command that has already finished has left it') beside blocks.read ('Read a window of one FINISHED command's output'). The split hands the model a choice it cannot make: it does not know whether the command has finished, and that is exactly the fact it is being asked to decide on. Measured cost, from the owner's screenshot: 'удали вот этот pdf' produced readScreen → blocks.list → blocks.read, three calls, to find what one block already held.

The state of execution is a FACT OF THE BLOCK and belongs in the answer, not in the choice of tool.

What makes this real work rather than a description edit: blocks.read executes InGo from the ledger, readScreen executes InRenderer through the broker, because a live command's output is in xterm and not in the ledger — AD-6 puts render state in the frontend and forbids the backend sniffing the stream. Executes is currently a property of the registry ROW (Declaration.Executes), so one tool whose execution site depends on the block's state is a change to that model.

A TOOL CALL IS A HEADER AND NOTHING ELSE. scrollback/blocks.ts:265-280: kind 'tool' has outputClass null, statusChips null, headerRight { chips: [], terminal: () => null }, and style.css:945-971 paints it as a margin note. The comment states the reason — 'the call's result has an owner already (the ledger's attempt)' and 'a chip here would be a second, later-arriving owner of an outcome this surface never receives'. That is the point: the renderer is NOT SENT the outcome. So this is a wire change first (the outcome and the duration must reach the renderer), and a rendering change second. ADR-0037 must be amended in the same commit that changes it, deliberately — not routed around.
acceptance_criteria:
ONE TOOL. A person asks about a command that is still running and about one that finished, in the same session. The assistant reads both through the SAME tool, addressing each block by id, and the answer tells it which state the block is in — running, or exited with a code. No question forces the model to choose a tool by whether the command has finished.

EVERY CALL ACCOUNTS FOR ITSELF. In a turn that made several calls, each call's row shows how long it took and how it ended, in the same vocabulary a command's block uses, and a call that failed is visibly distinct from one that succeeded. Watched end to end by one automated check.

## Deliberately out
- Rendering a tool call's full result as block output. What the row gains is the OUTCOME and the duration; whether the result body is shown is a separate decision, deliberately not taken here.
- Removing readScreen's remaining job (a full-screen program on the alternate buffer owns the screen and is not a block at all) unless the owner decides that case is out of scope — see the design question in the child bead.

title: A block that is working says so, wherever the work is
description:
Two defects the owner found on 2026-08-24.

THE INDICATOR. The turn's typing dots (scrollback/blocks.ts:2176-2183) are a one-shot stand-in for an EMPTY answer body: stopTyping (:2217) removes them at the first thing the turn draws — first tool call (:2303), first reasoning chunk (:2367), first delta (via stopWaiting) — and nothing ever puts them back. So a turn that spends 28 seconds inside a tool shows nothing at all where its answer will be written; only the header chip and pulse report. A running COMMAND has no dots at all: createRunningBlock (:1275-1321) builds no body, because the body of a running command is the live xterm region, which is a sibling of the blocks in .scrollback-inner.

The constraint that makes this non-trivial and must be honoured: style.css:975-979 requires the live region and the frozen body it becomes to occupy the SAME height, 'or the pane moves at the moment one replaces the other'.

THE MENU. buildOverflowMenu positions fixed at btnRect.bottom + 2 with no viewport clamp and no flip (scrollback/blocks.ts:1038-1042); .cmd-overflow-menu (style.css:1175) has neither max-height nor overflow. A running block sits at the bottom of the scrollback by construction, so 'Ask about this command' and 'Stop' — the two items that only exist while it runs — are off-screen almost always. The kit already owns this: ui/context-menu.tsx:100-118 clamps on both axes with EDGE_MARGIN_PX. Two implementations of one concept; the second one is wrong.
acceptance_criteria:
One indicator, one owner, both kinds of block. A person asks a question whose turn calls a tool that takes seconds: from the moment the question is sent until the moment the answer's first word lands, the place the answer will be written shows the working indicator — including the whole time the tool is running. They run a command that prints nothing for seconds: the same indicator stands where its output will appear, and it is the SAME markup, not a second one that looks similar. Neither indicator survives the first byte, and neither survives a failure. Watched end to end by one automated check.

Separately: the bottom-most block on screen has its ⋮ menu opened and every item is fully visible inside the viewport, with no scrolling and no clipping.

## Deliberately out
- Progress, percentages or a spinner per tool call. This is 'something is happening here', nothing more.

title: The assistant's answer reads like a document, not like a stream
description:
Three defects found by the owner on 2026-08-24, all in the answer renderer, all visible in one screenshot.

The renderer paints ONE COMPLETED LINE at a time (frontend/src/ui/answer-markdown.ts:8-27) because the answer body is a stack of .term-line rows that selection, copy and the reference chips all stand on. That contract is right and this epic keeps it; what it does not keep is the three costs that turned out not to be inherent:

1. The hanging indent for list markers is padding-left + negative text-indent (styles/components/answer-markdown.css:45-48). text-indent is INHERITED and .ui-md-marker is an inline-block — a block container — so the -1.2em applies a second time, inside the marker's own box. The glyph lands left of .cmd-children's padding and is clipped by its border-left (style.css:923-925). Bullets and ordered numbers both.
2. inlineHtml (answer-markdown.ts:84-101) does not recurse: the alternation takes the whole **...** token and escapes its contents as text, so **`repos`** prints literal backticks while `repos` on its own renders as a chip. Two spellings of one concept in one answer.
3. Fenced code is on the deliberately-unrendered list because it spans lines. A minimal multi-line accumulator is enough for it alone, and the kit's CodeBlock has no copy button for anyone.
acceptance_criteria:
A person asks a question whose answer contains a bulleted list, a numbered list, a word in bold with inline code inside it, and a fenced code block. Every list marker — bullet or number — sits in its own column INSIDE the block and never crosses its left rail. The code inside the bold renders as a code chip, not as literal backticks. The fenced block renders as ONE formatted unit with a copy button that puts exactly its text (no fences) on the clipboard. Watched end to end by one automated check.

## Deliberately out
- Tables, setext headings, nested block quotes, horizontal rules, images, task lists — the other things answer-markdown.ts names as deliberately unrendered. Only the fenced code block graduates here.
- Links becoming anchors: answer-markdown.ts refuses that on purpose (the model chooses the target) and this epic does not reopen it.

title: The header's plus makes the request beside the one you are in, not at the root
description:
Reported by the owner: with a request open inside a folder, the header's New
request (#api-new-request) writes to the collection ROOT. The crumb trail
directly above the control says `acme-api > users > create`, so the button
contradicts the line it sits in.

The precedent is `duplicateRequest`, which already lands the copy "BESIDE THE
ORIGINAL" using `directoryOf(relPath)`. The header's plus is the only door
that ignores where the person is; the folder row's menu already passes its
own path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a collection with a request inside a folder (`users/create.json`).
2. Click that request, so the header reads `acme-api > users > create`.
3. Press the plus in the header.
4. The new request appears at the collection root, not under `users/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `users/create.json` open, pressing New request calls `writeRequest`
  with `users/untitled-request.json`.
- With nothing in the form, it still writes to the collection root.
- With the workbench pointed at a DIFFERENT collection from the open
  request, it writes to that collection's root — the open request's folder
  belongs to another tree.
close_reason: The header's plus reads an omitted folder as 'here': newRequest(dir?) falls back to the open request's folder inside the ACTIVE collection. Watched at the seam a person presses (api-workbench.test.tsx) and at the store, including the cross-collection guard. 446 api tests green, pre-commit gate green. 7165856b

title: The shell JSON decoder drops a character: 2>&1 becomes 2>1 and writes a file named 1
description:
Found by a worker fixing the e2e container residue (nocx-qkid5) on 2026-08-24, while accounting for every file a run leaves behind. It is not a container defect — it happens on every real machine.

internal/shellintegration/scripts/nocx.bash:517-521 converts \uXXXX to octal so one printf %b pass decodes it with everything else:

    printf -v oct '%03o' "$((16#$hex))"
    s="${s//\\u$hex/\\$oct}"

For & (\u0026) that yields the three-digit form \046. But bash's %b reads \0nnn — a backslash, a ZERO, then up to three octal digits. Given \046 it takes the 0 as the marker, then 46, then EATS THE NEXT CHARACTER as the third octal digit. So \0461 is one character, not two, and the 1 is gone.

Measured at the shell:

    printf '%b' '2>\0461'    ->  2>1      (the & and the 1 collapse into one byte)
    printf '%b' '2>\00461'   ->  2>&1     (the four-digit form is correct)

The observable consequence: the far shell's bootstrap loader ships 2>&1 and receives 2>1, so its stderr is redirected to a FILE NAMED 1 in whatever directory the loader runs from. A 0-byte file named '1' had been sitting untracked in this worktree for the whole session and was dismissed as a shell typo by a human and by an agent; it was the product writing it.

Two reasons this is P1 rather than tidy-up. Any \uXXXX followed by a digit silently loses a character in an rcfile the product executes — the corruption is arbitrary, not limited to this one sequence. And a redirection that was meant to discard stderr instead creates a file in the user's working directory, which is a write nobody asked for, on every host the shell integration reaches.

The fix is the leading zero (\\0%03o), but the test is the point: the pass has never had one that puts a digit after an escape.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. printf '%b' '2>\0461'  ->  '2>1'
2. Start a shell-integration bootstrap on any host and look for a 0-byte file named '1' in the loader's cwd.
acceptance_criteria:
- The \uXXXX pass emits a form printf %b cannot over-consume. Reproduced at the shell: printf '%b' '2>\\0461' gives '2>1'; printf '%b' '2>\\00461' gives '2>&1'.
- A test decodes a JSON string containing \u0026 followed by a digit and asserts the exact result. It must FAIL before the fix.
- The same test covers the neighbours: any \uXXXX whose octal is followed by a digit, and one whose octal is followed by a non-digit (which works today and must keep working).
- No file named '1' appears in the cwd after a shell-integration bootstrap on a normal machine.

title: A backend from an older build refuses a newer frontend, and says how to fix it
description:
A backend that outlives its window also outlives an upgrade: yesterday's daemon serving today's frontend is the ordinary case, not the edge one.

AD-1 allocated a version byte and the control plane is JSON-RPC, so the skew is expressible. What is missing is the policy. Refusing is honest and cheap; a live handoff is what herdr does (it carries handoff.rs and exports live PTYs to a replacement server) and is a great deal more work.

Whatever is chosen, the failure must be legible: a user who upgraded and cannot connect needs to be told to restart the backend, not shown a connection error.

Related and not the same: nocx-1p1h4, 'A worker survives the network, and an upgrade never strands one'.
acceptance_criteria:
A frontend meeting a backend of an incompatible version is told so, in the product, with the action that fixes it.
A compatible pair connects with no prompt.
The refusal is distinguishable from a transient connection failure, so the client does not retry a mismatch forever.

title: nocx finds a running backend at startup, or starts one
description:
herdr's ordering: the server comes up first, the UI attaches to it. For nocx this is the frontend's Backend seam from phase A of this epic, pointed at a backend that happens to be on this machine but not in this process.

Needs: a socket path, named sessions so more than one can exist, and a handshake that establishes this is our backend and not somebody else's. Starting one when none is running, and not starting two when the user opens two windows.
acceptance_criteria:
Launching nocx with no backend running starts one and attaches.
Launching a second window attaches to the same backend rather than starting a second.
A stale socket from a crashed backend does not prevent a new one from starting.

title: The backend does not exit when the window closes
description:
Most of this is already true and that is the point. Session lifetime is already detached from connection lifetime — internal/transport/ws_git.go:24 says bindings 'are bounded by the session, not the WebSocket, so a reconnect' keeps them, and ring.go:35 keeps the replay ring 'stored connection-independently so the ring survives a disconnect'. A dropped client does not kill a PTY today.

What kills it is the process exiting, because the backend is in-process with the Wails shell. So this task is 'do not exit', not 'rewrite ownership of processes' — and cmd/devharness already proves the headless target runs the real backend with no wails, no GTK and no display.

The consequence to settle rather than inherit: the 2026-08-15 design's D5 says stage-1 workers die with the backend. That decision made sense while the backend was tied to a window and does not survive this task.
acceptance_criteria:
Closing the window leaves running processes running, and reopening finds them.
A long-running command started before the window closed is still producing output afterwards, and that output is recorded.
D5 of the workspaces design is revisited explicitly and the new answer is written down.

title: The client that attached last becomes active, and the channel resizes to it
description:
herdr's rule, and the reason attaching from a second machine feels right rather than cramped: on connect the newcomer becomes the foreground client (src/server/headless.rs:3027) and the shared runtime is resized to it immediately. The active client therefore always fits exactly, because it is the one that defined the size.

This is deliberately NOT tmux's smallest-common-size. Choosing the minimum makes every client wrong except the smallest; choosing the active one makes the client you are looking at right, always.
acceptance_criteria:
Attaching from a second client resizes the session to that client, and a program running in the pane reflows.
Returning to the first client resizes back.
Detaching every client leaves the session at its last size or the default, and does not kill it.

title: effectiveSize is a session property, owned by the backend
description:
Move the decision, not the measurement. The client still measures itself — only a webview knows its font metrics and pane geometry — but open stops SETTING the channel size and starts REPORTING the client's window size. The backend decides.

With no client attached the session holds a named default rather than having no size, which is what a backend outliving its window needs (nocx-if6).

AD-1's letter survives: the channel is still created at its final size and never spawned-then-resized. What changes is who chose that size.
acceptance_criteria:
A session created with no client attached has the default size and a working channel.
A client attaching reports its geometry and the backend, not the client, sets the channel size.
The contract in contracts/ is updated in the same commit and the generated renderer types match it.

title: A client asks for output older than the replay ring and gets it
description:
The ring is 256 KB, about ten screens (internal/transport/ring.go:14), and is deliberately not scrollback. Today that is the whole of what a reattaching client can recover, so a client that joins an hour into a run sees ten screens of it.

The client asks by offset — it already speaks that coordinate system for AD-9 acks — and renders what comes back with its own VT, at the session's size. So the same bytes plus the same size give the same screen, which is what makes two clients agree without a grid on the backend.

Block boundaries are not re-derived here: they are already the backend's, from the lifecycle channel.
acceptance_criteria:
A client attaching an hour into a session recovers output from before the ring window.
Two clients attached to the same session render the same content.
A request for an offset that has been dropped by the retention bound answers with what remains and says what is missing, rather than silently returning less.

title: Session output is written durably by the backend, not held only by the renderer
description:
The backend already holds every byte — it reads the PTY or the SSH channel and forwards it — and it already keys them by offset for the AD-9 replay ring. What it does not do is keep them.

Recording is geometry-free: a byte stream has no width, so nothing here needs a size, a grid, or a VT. And it interprets nothing, so AD-6 is untouched: storing what you already forward is not sniffing it.

The bound must exist from the first commit rather than be added after somebody fills a disk, and it is not this task's to invent: nocx-2f0f.5 already shipped the user-facing budget — four knobs and an eviction path — for the artifacts the renderer captures. Reuse it. nocx-jrdy is a DIFFERENT concern and an earlier revision of this bead named it for the wrong one: jrdy is 'nothing is kept that you did not mean to keep', the SECRET-bearing half of a durable ledger. It matters here more than it did there, not less — a raw byte stream retains everything the PTY echoed, including what the renderer would never have serialized into a block body, so the printed-secret half of jrdy's design gets larger the moment this lands.
acceptance_criteria:
Output produced while no client is attached is on disk afterwards.
The recorded stream replays to the same bytes the client received, checked by offset rather than by eye.
A bound exists on what is kept, and exceeding it drops oldest-first and says so rather than failing a write.

title: N workers, a routing table, and the queue that gets what is left
description:
Fan-out to N, and the design question that decides whether any of this is useful: which facts are routine, which wake the coordinator, and which go to the human.

Get it wrong and the attention queue becomes noise, which is the failure nocx-ms7v.4 warns about in its own description. Routine facts — a worker started, a worker finished with two still running — are recorded and wake nobody. Judgement facts — a worker asks, a worker crashed, two workers claim the same files — wake the coordinator. What the coordinator does not dispatch within a named deadline reaches the human.

Escalation must coalesce per wave rather than per fact, or five workers finishing while the coordinator is away produce five identical cards. And a fact the coordinator picks up late must clear its own escalation: nocx-ms7v.4 says resolved is only an explicit act, which is right, and this makes the coordinator a second actor performing it — a change to that bead, not merely a use of it.

THIS IS WHERE THE NUMBER COMES FROM. What fraction of facts reaches the coordinator rather than the human is the measure of whether this design works; if most escalate, the mechanism moved the work to the human and should be said so out loud.
acceptance_criteria:
Three workers run; a routine completion wakes nobody, a question wakes the coordinator, and an unread fact reaches the attention queue naming the worker and how long it has waited.
Five facts arriving while the coordinator is away produce one escalation, not five.
A coordinator that picks up a fact after escalation clears that escalation itself.
The escalated fraction is measured and reported, not assumed.

title: The backend wakes the coordinator when a fact needs it
description:
The coordinator being idle is the normal state, not the failure. What must be true is that a fact needing judgement reaches it without anyone remembering anything.

The general route is the keystroke from the sibling task: the backend types into the coordinator's pane, which starts a turn. Locally the backend does it; on a remote host the helper does it on the far side, so nothing leaves the machine.

The route must be honest about what it is: delivery is unacknowledged, so waking never closes a fact. Only the coordinator's own subsequent call does.

And a wake costs the coordinator tokens, so it happens only when there is an undispatched fact — which is also why a per-fact deadline, rather than a lease, is the right shape for the backstop: nothing ticks while there is nothing to dispatch.
acceptance_criteria:
A coordinator that has been idle for minutes is woken by the backend when a worker declares completion, and takes a turn without the user touching anything.
A wave with no undispatched facts wakes nobody, and no timer is running.
A wake that cannot be delivered — no free_text, no observer, a dead pane — is recorded with its reason rather than reported as sent.

title: The wave record: one coordinator, one worker, and the backend is what watches
description:
The defect this epic exists for is that a coordinator forgets it has children, and five entries in this repository's memories are five faces of it. The cure is not a better protocol for the agent to follow. An agent exists only while it takes a turn, so ANYTHING that depends on an act the agent must remember is not an invariant — and that holds against every upstream fix, including Claude Code's Monitor tool, which is durable across turns and still has to be armed.

So supervision moves out of the agent entirely. The backend is a process without turns: it holds the wave record, and it cannot forget. An earlier draft made supervision a LEASE the coordinator holds and renews; that was still an act, and its renewal was a poll by another name.

Start with ONE worker, not three. Three is the demonstration; one is the mechanism, and fan-out is cheap once one works.

The record's facts come from sources that already exist: process exit (internal/procwatch, and the channel's exit status for a remote pane) and the participant's own declaration over the authenticated channel (ADR-0024 decision 2). Never from the screen — the grid decides typing and lighting, and nothing else.

Remote works from day one and needs no helper change: the bytes of a remote pane already pass through the backend, because that is how the terminal works.
acceptance_criteria:
A coordinator in a nocx pane starts one worker, gives it a task, and goes idle — with the wave still supervised and no alarm raised.
The worker finishes; the backend records both its declaration and its process exit, and neither alone terminalizes it.
An automated check watches the whole sequence end to end.
Killing the coordinator between turns does not lose the worker, and a fresh coordinator asks what it holds and is told by name.

title: nocx types into a pane, and only when the driver says it may
description:
Waking an agent means starting a turn it did not ask for. The general mechanism — the one that works for every agent rather than for one vendor — is a keystroke into the pane, which nocx can send because it owns the PTY.

What makes it safe is not mitigation but refusal: type only on free_text. An earlier draft of this design proposed sending Escape first to make a mistimed keystroke recoverable; that is strictly worse than nelix's answer, which is to not type at all unless the state is positively identified. A mistimed keystroke does not merely fail to deliver — it answers whatever modal is on screen, which can approve a tool call the user never saw.

Actuation details are the driver's, not the caller's: framing a submission as a bracketed paste, pressing the submit key SEPARATELY so it cannot be swallowed as paste content, and selecting a numbered option with the digit. nelix measured the paste framing at 0.0s against 2.2s for raw echo on 61.5 KB.

Delivery here is UNACKNOWLEDGED: seeing our text echo in the input region is evidence it was typed, never that it was acted on. So a keystroke never closes anything by itself — only the participant's own subsequent call does.
acceptance_criteria:
A pane in free_text receives the text and a separate submit key, and the text appears in the input region and not in scrollback.
A pane showing a permission menu, a working spinner, or an unknown state receives nothing at all, and the refusal is recorded with the reason.
A pane nocx did not launch receives nothing until a full repaint has been observed.

title: The indicator reads the driver, and three workers show three states
description:
This is what makes the grid and the driver reachable rather than dead code, and it is the epic's own deliverable: three workers stop collapsing into one dot.

Today the indicator is one boolean per pane — Pane._hasActivity, in frontend/src/PANES.ts (this bead first said tabs.ts:52; that file was renamed by nocx-ehkvy on 2026-08-17, a week before the bead was written). Its markActivity() is guarded exactly as described: it returns early while the pane is active, because setActive() clears the flag on activation and not on deactivation.

The 'no provenance' half is now only half true, and the difference matters because it means the model to extend already exists. agent-status.ts is still a stateless title classifier, but nocx-n3nfg wrapped it: pane-work-finished.ts holds the working -> idle edge for a settle window and raises pane.workFinished at trust: heuristic, and internal/notify's Trust is a three-class capability enforced default-deny — heuristic may never reach a sink that leaves the machine (notify.go:355). So the driver's classification does not need a NEW provenance vocabulary. It needs to be stamped into the shipped one, and the two things this bead adds on top are attempt-binding and a named source, neither of which Trust carries. The driver's classification replaces the guess for panes that have one, and the title-derived value stays for panes that do not — on the weaker provenance row, where it may light the indicator and decide nothing.

Provenance travels with the observation: every one is attempt-bound, so a late observation from a previous incarnation cannot overwrite a current one.
acceptance_criteria:
Three AGENT PANES in three different states — one working, one waiting on a permission prompt, one exited — show three distinct indicators at the same time. Started by hand, not by a wave: nocx-dkawo depends on this epic, so requiring a wave here would make the epic unfinishable (corrected 2026-08-25 with the rest of the f5ef47e1 edge reversal).
Activating a tab does not erase what its indicator was reporting.
A pane with no driver still lights from the title, and is marked as the weaker source.
close_reason: The indicator reads the driver. Three panes in three states are three distinct data-agent-status values on screen at once, asserted through the whole renderer chain in panes.test.ts; activating a tab clears its unread-output mark and leaves what the pane is doing alone; a pane with no driver still lights from the title and carries data-agent-source=title.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text: Landed with nocx-szb40.3, which is what its comment said would happen. The indicator now reads pane-observation.ts, which is the single owner of the merge: a driver observation displaces the title entirely (including its 'unknown' — 'this screen could not be read' beats a confident wrong answer), and the title stays for every pane with no driver, marked data-agent-source=title and drawn at lower opacity. agentStatus was WIDENED rather than joined by a second field: PaneActivity extends AgentStatus with waiting/unknown/exited, so the tab, the overview card and the workspace chip all follow the strong source without a second vocabulary. Activating a tab clears the unread-output mark and does not touch what the pane is doing — asserted. The epic's deliverable is proven end to end in panes.test.ts: three panes, three fired observations, three distinct data-agent-status values on screen at once.

title: A driver classifies pane state into a closed set, and refuses to guess
description:
The idea is taken from nelix's driver (daemon/drivers/claude.py, and its Driver protocol in base.py) — the idea, not the code. What makes it work is worth restating because each part was bought:

ONE closed set of outcomes: free_text, permission_choice, modal_choice, none (working), unknown, plus crash/exit taken from the process rather than the screen. Anything ambiguous is 'unknown', and unknown is treated as busy.

TWO markers, never one: the input marker AND the prompt footer. A stray prompt glyph in scrollback is not an input box.

ORDER IS A SAFETY PROPERTY: the modal-menu branch is evaluated BEFORE the free-text branch, so a permission prompt can never be masked by the input box that is still on screen beneath it.

ANCHORED IN CHROME, NEVER IN THE AGENT'S OUTPUT. nelix's comment calls this injection safety. It is also the cure for a failure this repository measured: a completion sentinel that matched itself at 7-13 seconds because the agent printed the brief it had just read.

AND THE SUBAGENT TRAP: Claude keeps the input box live while its main turn is blocked on a background subagent. A stable frame with a visible prompt is NOT idle.

Per AD-8 this is an interface with one implementation per agent, and the registry fails closed for an unregistered or partial driver.


INHERITED FROM nocx-szb40.2, and it is an obligation rather than a note. The grid exists and is fed from the backend's read path, but NOTHING ENROLS A PANE IN PRODUCTION: the enrolment act is a Go seam, and deadcode -whylive confirms the shape — Store.Feed traces to main, while Store.Frame and Frame.Text come back 'reachable only through reflection'. So this task carries two things beyond classification. It must bring session.observe (the wire method, its schema in contracts/, and its generated renderer type) TOGETHER WITH THE CALLER that makes it non-dead — the frontend's dead-export ratchet refused the contract without one, correctly, and its baseline may only shrink. And it is the first reader of a Frame. If this task stalls, nocx-szb40.2's grid is a write path with no caller, which is nocx-rtg0's own failure, and it should be removed rather than left looking wired.

TWO INTEGRATION FACTS already paid for, in internal/panegrid: feed the emulator with Write and never InputPipe (that is the keyboard side and returns an empty grid), and its replies must be drained or Write blocks. Both are handled inside the package; a second caller reaching for the emulator directly would have to repeat them, which is a reason not to.
acceptance_criteria:
The classifier returns one value from the closed set for every frame, and an ambiguous frame returns unknown.
A frame showing a permission menu over a live input box classifies as the menu, not as free text.
A frame in which the agent has printed text resembling a prompt or a completion classifies from chrome alone and is unaffected by it.
A pane blocked on a background subagent while its input box is visible does not classify as accepting input.
close_reason: The classifier landed with the wire and the caller that makes it non-dead. Five states off five real captures, every anchor a position, and the two markers are the box's rules and the cursor — a forged dialog printed into the transcript does not move the verdict. The inherited obligation is discharged: panegrid.Store.Frame and Frame.Text now trace to main under deadcode -whylive. Not session.observe — see the comment above: the enrolment act has no renderer caller, so what crosses is session.observationChanged, a change plus a replay on reattach.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
The captures this task needs are taken and committed: spike/vt-agreement/captures/ holds real claude TUI byte streams for the idle input box, a turn in flight, a Write permission dialog, the /model modal and the subagent trap, with spike/vt-agreement/bin/frameat to replay one to any millisecond mark.

Three findings from them, before any code:

The permission dialog uses the SAME glyph as the input marker — its selected row is '❯ 1. Yes' — and it REPLACES the input box rather than overlaying it. So 'two markers, never one' is not a precaution here, it is the difference between refusing and approving a tool call the user never saw.

The subagent trap reproduced exactly as the bead predicts, and its chrome is narrower than expected: input box live, footer present, NO spinner, and the only signal that the turn is blocked is the mode-line segment '· /tasks to see subagents ·'. A rule written from 'input box and no spinner means idle' classifies a blocked agent as ready for input.

The spinner is chrome by POSITION, not by content: it sits directly above the token-counter row, which sits directly above the input box's top rule. The same glyph and wording appear in the transcript afterwards ('✻ Brewed for 4s') and must not match — which is the anchoring rule paying for itself on the first capture.

This task now depends on nocx-szb40.5, which is the enrolment act it was written to carry, and lands together with nocx-szb40.4, which is the only consumer its classification has.

comments.author: shady2k
comments.text:
Landed. Three of this bead's own recorded findings were wrong, and the corpus
is what said so — each correction is in the code beside the rule it changed.

THE SPINNER IS NOT AT A FIXED OFFSET, and position alone does not separate a
live spinner from a finished one. It sits in the status stack — the contiguous
run of rows directly above the token meter — and that stack GROWS: with a tip
line present the spinner is three rows above the input box's top rule rather
than two (claude-subagent at 42s). And the turn's closing summary occupies the
same slot and stays there: '✻ Sautéed for 29s' holds it from 46s to the end,
long after the turn ended. So the stack decides WHERE to look and the grammar
decides WHAT was found — a live spinner carries '… (' and closes its
parenthesis, a finished one never does.

THE SUBAGENT TRAP HAS TWO CHROME FORMS, NOT ONE, AND AN END. From 25s to 38s
the only signal is a task panel drawn UNDER the mode line ('● main' over '◯
Explore …'); the '· /tasks to see subagents ·' segment only appears at 40s.
And it is live evidence rather than a permanent hint — it is GONE by 70s when
the background agent finished and the pane is genuinely waiting. A rule with
only the segment misses half the interval; a rule without its second end
leaves the pane refusing input for the rest of the session.

THE CURSOR IS THE SECOND MARKER, and it is the one that cannot be forged. In
the approval dialog it sits ON the selected option's '❯' (1,26); in /model on
the same glyph (3,31); with a live input box it sits just after the marker.
An agent can print '❯ 1. Yes' into its transcript. It cannot take the cursor.
The menu branch anchors there, which is why a forged dialog in the transcript
cannot move the verdict.

One more the captures decided and nobody had asked: the input row's CONTENTS
are not evidence a human typed. 'now echo goodbye', 'wait for the results' and
"what's in caps?" appear in the input box of captures whose scripts sent none
of them — they are the agent's own suggested follow-ups.

WHAT LANDED, beyond the classifier: internal/paneobserve (classify a watched
pane, report only CHANGES, retain the state for a reattaching client), the
session.observationChanged notification with its schema and its generated
renderer type, and the renderer chain to the tab. Not session.observe: the
enrolment act belongs to the authenticated shell channel and the renderer
never performs it, so a method for it would have no caller — what crosses is
the classification, as a change plus a replay on reattach, which is the pair
this repository already uses (git.status/git.changed, files.list/files.changed).

The inherited obligation is discharged: deadcode -whylive now traces
panegrid.Store.Frame and panegrid.Frame.Text to main.

'exited' is produced by the WITHDRAWAL — the agent asking to stop being
watched is the one moment nocx knows a process is gone rather than inferring
it from a screen — and it is terminal and retained, because the shell keeps
repainting underneath and the next classification would be about the shell.

title: The backend keeps a live grid for a participant pane, and the boundary is written down
description:
A TUI sends diffs, not full repaints, so a frame cannot be reconstructed from the tail of the stream. Observation therefore needs a LIVE grid, fed continuously — not a stateless transformer, which is what an earlier draft of this design claimed and which is false.

Scope: ENROLLED panes only, from enrolment to the terminal record, then discarded. Enrolment is an explicit control-plane act naming a pane, never an inference that a pane's title looks like an agent — an inferred set has no upper bound and no audit. A wave participant is one producer of an enrolment; a person starting an agent in a pane is another, and that second one is what makes this epic finishable, since nocx-dkawo depends on it (corrected 2026-08-25 with the rest of the f5ef47e1 edge reversal; this said 'panes of a live wave only'). Ordinary tabs are untouched and their indicator stays where it is today (frontend/src/agent-status.ts). One grid per participant pane, fed from bytes that already pass through the backend.

Because nocx launches the participant itself, the grid starts at byte zero of that process and never has to guess at state accumulated before it was watching. A pane adopted rather than launched has no such guarantee: until a full repaint is seen its state is 'unknown', which is refused for typing. herdr hit the same wall on server handoff and answers it with a resize nudge (headless.rs:341, 'Imported panes get one app-safe resize nudge after the first client attaches') — usable when adopting, never as the mechanism.

THIS BREAKS AD-6, and not narrowly: the backend begins deriving meaning from the byte stream, which AD-6's own amendment refuses by name ('a read that needs the stream to mean something — a marker, a prompt ... is refused by this bullet'). ADR-0002 closed the same door twice in its Consequences, and the two halves are SEPARATE bullets rather than one passage: 'AD-6 stands. No VT grid on the Go side; render state stays in the frontend' (line 42), and, of zellij's 'server holds the grid and repaints on attach', that the alternative 'is closed to us by AD-6, not merely unchosen — worth recording so it is not re-proposed as a shortcut' (lines 47-49, and that one is about the reconnect ring, not the grid). An earlier revision of this bead quoted them spliced with an ellipsis that read as continuous; the substance holds either way. Its revisit trigger — 'remote-persistent sessions become a product requirement … a session that survives the client process entirely', which ADR-0002 itself calls an AD-level change and not a UI decision — has now fired.

So the boundary goes into docs/architecture.md beside AD-6 in the same shape as its existing carve-out: an interval with both ends, and an explicit statement of what it does NOT license. The grid may decide exactly two things — may nocx write to this pane, and what the indicator shows. It may never decide wave state, a lifecycle attempt, or an execution attempt; that authority stays with the authenticated channel (ADR-0024 decision 2) and with process exit.



LIBRARY CHOSEN, nocx-szb40.1: github.com/charmbracelet/x/vt, measured in spike/vt-agreement/REPORT.md. It is the only candidate that reproduces xterm.js's COLUMN GEOMETRY across a double-width character — hinshun/vt10x's Glyph has no width field at all, so it packs a wide character into one column and everything to its right shifts left. Both powers this bead grants the grid are positional, so that mattered more than the text fidelity on which the two were tied.

TWO INTEGRATION FACTS from that measurement, both of which cost time to find:
1. The emulator DEADLOCKS unless something drains its Read side. It replies upstream — device attributes and friends — and a real terminal always has a reader. Feed it with Write, not InputPipe: InputPipe is the KEYBOARD side, and using it returns a completely empty grid rather than an error.
2. Its continuation cell for the second column of a wide character is a SPACE at width 0, where xterm.js writes an empty string. Any consumer reading text off the grid must skip w==0 cells or it injects a space after every wide character.
acceptance_criteria:
A participant pane has a backend grid fed from byte zero, and closing the frontend does not stop it being fed.
The amendment beside AD-6 names the interval's start and end, the two things the grid may decide, and the three it may not.
A test asserts that no wave state, lifecycle attempt or execution attempt can be opened, completed or altered from the grid.
ADR-0002 is marked superseded in part and points at the amendment, rather than being left reading as accepted while its own revisit trigger has fired.
close_reason: The backend keeps a live VT grid for an enrolled pane, on charmbracelet/x/vt, fed from pumpToRing — the per-session goroutine that lives connection-independently, so 'closing the frontend does not stop it being fed' is a property of the placement and is proved by a test that closes the websocket and then emits more bytes. The AD-6 amendment is in docs/architecture.md with the interval's both ends, the two powers and the three refusals, and ADR-0002 is marked superseded in part beside the consequence it corrects. The third criterion is asserted structurally: boundary_test.go parses the package's own imports and fails if it can reach lifecycle, session, content, notify or transport, with a companion test proving the walk is not vacuous. Commits f8e43c82 (amendment), 7063aaa4 (the half-applied edge reversal this uncovered), 7870897a (the code). WHAT IS NOT DONE, carried to nocx-szb40.3 as an obligation: nothing enrols a pane in production. session.observe was written with its schema and generated type and REMOVED from the commit, because the frontend's dead-export ratchet refused a contract type nobody imports and its baseline may only shrink — a contract lands with its caller. deadcode -whylive says the same in the other direction: Store.Feed traces to main, Store.Frame and Frame.Text are 'reachable only through reflection'. The write path is wired, the read path is not, and if szb40.3 stalls this is dead weight that should come out.

title: Choose the VT library by measuring real captures, not by reputation
description:
The backend needs a grid to know what an agent pane is doing. Three candidates to check (none is in go.mod today): github.com/hinshun/vt10x, github.com/charmbracelet/x/vt, github.com/tonistiigi/vt100.

Do NOT choose on features. The bar is agreement with xterm.js on real agent output, and it is different for the two consumers: for a frame the only thing that matters is the CHROME ANCHORS (input line, prompt footer, spinner, menu rows); for block text it is content fidelity. The second bar is far higher, so a library that fails it can still carry observation.

Known to break naive parsers, all of them things Claude actually emits: alternate screen, scroll regions, wide characters and braille spinners, and a NBSP (U+00A0) between the prompt marker and '[Pasted text #N]' — nelix's driver carries a comment saying a literal space silently misses it, found from a live capture.

Capture real streams from a real agent pane; do not synthesise them.
acceptance_criteria:
A recorded byte stream from a live agent pane is rendered by xterm.js and by the candidate, and the two frames are diffed.
The report says where they disagree and whether any disagreement touches a chrome anchor.
A candidate is chosen and the reason is one sentence naming the measurement, not the library's reputation.
close_reason: Chosen: github.com/charmbracelet/x/vt. It is the only candidate that reproduces xterm.js's column geometry across a double-width character, and a chrome anchor is a thing at a position. Measured in spike/vt-agreement/REPORT.md, commit d3872462, against a ground truth pinned to what the product ships (@xterm/headless 5.5.0 + unicode11, matching frontend/package.json and renderers/xterm.ts:334). Corpus is six captures of real programs on a real PTY, nothing synthesised: claude's first-run TUI (CHA x123, menus, spinner, input line), bash+bd, htop, vim, less, and less positioned on a CJK line. tonistiigi/vt100 is out on every non-trivial capture — 40.60% of cells and 0 of 8 chrome anchors on the Claude capture, cursor off the grid. vt10x and x/vt tie at 100% on all five narrow captures and split on the CJK line: vt10x's Glyph has no width field, so its columns drift left on every wide character, while x/vt's only difference from xterm is spelling the continuation cell as a space instead of an empty string, which a consumer normalises by skipping w==0. NOT COVERED, and named in the report rather than implied: no braille spinner, no OSC title, no NBSP before a pasted-text marker, no mid-work permission prompt, and attributes collected but not scored. Two harness bugs of mine are kept in the report because each would have produced a confident wrong answer: feeding x/vt through InputPipe (empty grid), and capturing htop/vim/less WITH their quit key, which compared restored blank screens where all three candidates agreed on nothing.

title: Two machines, one session, the same screen
description:
Today exactly one client can be attached meaningfully, because the frontend OWNS the size: AD-1 says 'open MUST carry initial {cols, rows, xpixel, ypixel}' and the channel is created at that size. Two clients of different sizes have no defined behaviour, and a session with no client has no size at all — which is what a backend outliving its window (nocx-if6) needs.

herdr answers this and its answer is not tmux's. src/server/headless.rs:329: 'Shared pane runtime size derived from the foreground client, or MIN_COLS x MIN_ROWS when no clients are connected'; sync_foreground_client_state sets effective_size from that ONE client; and on connect (headless.rs:3027) the newcomer becomes foreground and the runtime resizes to it. Rendering, meanwhile, is per client — clients.rs:288 render_targets carries each client's own terminal_size. Two sizes, two owners: the pane runtime is shared, the layout is each client's own.

For nocx the layout half is free (the UI is DOM, each window lays itself out). Only the pane runtime size moves. And because two clients then see the same bytes at the same size, they see the same screen WITHOUT a server-side grid — which is what keeps ADR-0002 intact.

AD-1's resize contract changes meaning, not letter: open stops SETTING the size and starts REPORTING the client's window size; the backend decides; the channel is still created at its final size, never spawned-then-resized.

DELIBERATELY OUT: reconciling two simultaneous clients by picking the smallest — deliberately not done, the active client wins and the other letterboxes.
acceptance_criteria:
Two clients attach to one session; both show the same content.
The client that attached last defines the size, and the channel resizes to it; the other renders at that size and pads or scrolls in its own window.
With no client attached the session keeps a named default size, and a client attaching later resizes it without losing the session.

title: The backend keeps the output, and it outlives the window
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-25, and read this first. This epic was created claiming to BE the epic nocx-rtg0 deferred to ('DELIBERATELY OUT: output capture (its own epic)'). It is not. That epic is nocx-2f0f, 'The terminal remembers what commands printed', and it is CLOSED — shipped 2026-08-19, eleven children, eight commits b3fa7685..65fca2dc. A frozen block's rows already leave the renderer as two artifacts (SGR + derived text) over ledger.capture and land in artifacts + artifact_chunks against the entry's own execution row (internal/transport/ws_ledger_capture.go, internal/content/ledger_sqlite.go, frontend/src/capture-client.ts). nocx-2f0f.5 shipped the byte budget with it: four knobs and an eviction path.

So this epic is NOT 'output capture is missing'. It is the half nocx-2f0f cannot reach by construction, and the distinction is the whole scope: 2f0f captures in the RENDERER at freeze time, so a session with no client attached captures NOTHING, and a block that never freezes has nothing to capture yet. That is precisely the case a backend outliving its window creates. Build ON the shipped path — same store, same provenance, same retention knobs — and never a second one beside it; if the recording genuinely cannot reuse it, say in the code why, per AGENTS.md.

Today the renderer owns the scrollback (AD-6) and the backend keeps only a bounded replay ring — internal/transport/ring.go:14, RingCapacity = 256 KB, about ten screens, and its own comment says 'The ring is NOT scrollback'. So output exists in exactly one place: the webview. Close it and everything past those ten screens was never anywhere else.

Two consumers make that untenable. A second client attaching to a live session gets ten screens of a two-hour run. And a backend that outlives its window (nocx-if6) records nothing at all while detached.

What this epic does NOT need: a VT on the backend. Recording a byte stream is geometry-free and interprets nothing, so AD-6 is untouched — the backend stores what it already holds and forwards. Block boundaries are already the authenticated lifecycle channel's (internal/lifecycle ExecutionAttempt carries Command, Cwd, Host, StartedAt, CompletedAt, ExitCode), never OSC 133 parsed on the backend, which AD-6 refuses by name.

DELIBERATELY OUT: derived text (the VT-rendered text of a block) stays the renderer's until a consumer for it exists; retention and budget policy, which nocx-jrdy owns.
acceptance_criteria:
A command produces more output than the replay ring holds; the window is closed and reopened, and the output before the last ten screens is still there.
A second client attaches to a live session an hour in and sees the same output as the first, not only the ring.
The backend never parses OSC 133: block boundaries come from the lifecycle channel, and a session with no shell integration records bytes and says out loud that it has no blocks.
The recording reuses the store and retention nocx-2f0f already ships, or the code says in place why it could not — there is not a second output store beside the first.

title: A tool call with no id loses the boundary: prose written before a command lands after it
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Drive one assistant turn where the model's first response carries BOTH prose and a `run`
tool call, and the call carries **no id**:

    fake.setScript({
      chunks: ['Let me check.'],
      toolCalls: [{ name: 'run', arguments: { sessionId, command: 'echo hello' } }],
    })
    fake.setScript({ chunks: ['Plenty.'] })

`e2e/agent-restore.spec.ts` does exactly this and is RED on it today.

## What happens

The turn draws TWO children where three are due:

    How much disk is free?                       126ms  completed
      ┌ agent  echo RAN-BY-THE-ASSISTANT-…         75ms      ok
      │ RAN-BY-THE-ASSISTANT-…
      Let me check.Plenty.

The two runs of prose are CONCATENATED into one block, and that block sits AFTER the
command. "Let me check." was written before the command and is drawn after it — which is
the defect ADR-0037 exists to make impossible, and the exact inversion nocx-shxv0 was opened
for, reappearing through a different door.

## The reproduction is deterministic, and it names the cause

Adding an id to the same call makes the same spec pass, first time, every time:

    toolCalls: [{ name: 'run', id: 'call_diag', arguments: {…} }]   → 1 passed
    toolCalls: [{ name: 'run',                  arguments: {…} }]   → 1 failed, 2 of 3 children

That is why `e2e/agent-turn.spec.ts` is green on the same shape: its calls carry
`id: 'call_run'` and `id: 'call_read'`.

## Where to look, and where NOT to

`ws_agent.go`'s seal path is not obviously at fault — it seals on any call whose prose block
is open, keyed on the block's entry id and not on the call's. The renderer dedupes on
`callId` (`seenCalls`), which for a single call with an empty id cannot suppress it. And the
command block IS adopted into the turn, so a call event certainly arrived.

So the ordering is lost upstream of both: find out whether the engine emits the tool call
before flushing the response's content, and whether an id-less call takes a different path
through it. Measure before theorising — the diff between the two specs is one field.

## Why it matters beyond the test

An id is the model's, not ours. A provider that omits one is not malformed, and the resume
path already treats the id as its identity key — so a run against such a provider would
silently draw every turn's prose in the wrong place. The product must not depend on the
model's bookkeeping to get its own ordering right.
acceptance_criteria:
- The scenario above renders three children in causal order — prose, command, prose — with
  the call carrying NO id. Asserted by `e2e/agent-restore.spec.ts` going green with the spec
  unchanged (no id added to make it pass).
- A unit test at the seam that actually loses the order asserts the same thing, so the
  regression is caught without a browser.
- Two calls that BOTH lack an id still render as two calls, not one: the renderer's `seenCalls`
  dedupe keys on the id, and an empty key is not an identity.
- `e2e/agent-turn.spec.ts` still passes, with its ids left as they are — a real provider sends
  them and that path must not regress while the id-less one is fixed.
close_reason:
Landed in 900d8716. The cause was not what the symptom pointed at. Two producers write one ordered stream: the engine's loop drains each model response on the CALLER's goroutine, and the policy middleware emits its AskToolCall from inside eino's tools node on the GRAPH's. A mutex serialized the writes and did not order them, so a response that both speaks and proposes a tool could deliver the call before the sentence preceding it; the transport seals the open prose block AT the call event, so a call arriving first found no block to seal and the prose either side merged. Fixed by emitting the response's chunks from a WrapModel wrapper, which the framework runs before the tools node can start, so "chunks first" stops being a race.

The renderer half landed with it and had to: terminal-content.ts dropped the blockId every delta carries, so the renderer re-derived the boundary from call announcements instead of reading the backend's stored fact. That second derivation is what hid this for as long as the calls happened to arrive conveniently. Landing either half alone makes the product worse, and it was measured rather than argued: with the renderer fix and without the engine fix, the end-to-end check goes green to red.

Three of my own hypotheses were wrong along the way and each was killed by a measurement rather than by argument. "The call id is missing, so the boundary is lost" — the id-less coverage the brief demanded was never red; the transport's boundary ignores the id entirely, and that test stays as the statement that it does. "The backend does not seal for an id-less call" — it seals unconditionally. "The symptom is the epic's last defect" — it had already been closed by 173001b9's empty-key dedupe fix, and the real defect only became visible once the renderer stopped covering for it.

Two worker windows, one WORKER_BLOCKED in between that was the coordinator's fault (dispatched onto a tree without the specs, because the e2e work was uncommitted). That worker still delivered: it measured the engine seam, found and fixed the empty-callId dedupe, and refused to invent a passing state.

Verified by the coordinator on the merged tree, not on the worker's: build clean, internal/assistant and internal/transport green, both tsconfigs clean, 521 frontend tests, and BOTH e2e specs green together with the renderer fix in place — which is the acceptance, not either alone.

title: [BUG] The 2026-08-15 design lets byte-stream facts decide agent state, which ADR-0024 forbids
description:
Found by adversarial review (codex, 2026-08-24) while reviewing
.internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md. The defect is in the OTHER
document, which is why this is filed separately rather than fixed in passing.

.internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md section 5.2 defines the
`observed` evidence class as "pty facts: exit, alternate screen, blocked on stdin, silence for N",
and that class is allowed to decide agent state.

ADR-0024 decision 1 says the opposite, and says it exhaustively: "No sequence parsed from the byte
stream — standard OSC, private OSC, DCS, title, terminal mode, or anything else — may grant DOM
keyboard ownership, declare prompt readiness, OPEN OR COMPLETE AN EXECUTION ATTEMPT, assign an
exit status, persist a history record, enable integration-sensitive command rewriting, or
authorize a re-run."

Alternate screen is a terminal mode read from the byte stream. The title is named outright. So two
of the four members of `observed` may not decide anything, and the row as written invites a
backend that infers from bytes — the exact class AD-6 exists to prevent.

The remaining two are weak for different reasons: silence is not a state at all, and
blocked-on-stdin is not trustworthily observable from a PTY (readability, foreground process group
and absence of output do not prove a process is waiting for a human).

Only PROCESS EXIT survives as an observed fact that may decide, and it survives because it is a
process fact rather than a stream fact.

The 2026-08-15 design is a second draft and is NOT approved, so this is cheap to fix now and
expensive once an epic is built on it. nocx-4n3bz's mechanism design takes the narrow position
(its D9) and records that it owes this amendment.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Read section 5.2 of .internal/specs/2026-08-15-workspaces-lineage-and-orchestration-design.md
   and note that the `observed` class lists alternate screen and is permitted to decide.
2. Read decision 1 of docs/decisions/0024-authenticated-shell-integration-channel.md, which names
   "terminal mode" and "title" among the things that may not open or complete an execution
   attempt.
3. The two cannot both hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Section 5.2 of the 2026-08-15 design distinguishes what an evidence class may DECIDE from what
  it may merely DISPLAY, and no byte-stream-derived source appears on the deciding side.
- The document states the ADR-0024 quotation as the reason, so the next reader does not re-open it.
- Falsified if any class that can be produced by a hostile file being `cat`ed can still open or
  complete an execution attempt.

title: Spawn-and-register has no transaction and no recovery: name the interval and both its ends
description:
Found by adversarial review (codex, 2026-08-24), unnamed failure mode A. Open question 5 of
.internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md.

Starting one participant is at least five steps: validate plan and authority; create the wave and
participant records; create the session/worktree and spawn the agent; enrol the process and stage
its surface; mark the participant live and take up supervision. The design states none of the
cuts, and AGENTS.md testing rule 3 is explicit that this is where the defects are.

The cuts, each of which leaves a different world:

- after the record, before the process: a durable participant with nothing behind it;
- after the spawn, before the record commits: a live agent nobody owns;
- after the session, before enrolment: an ordinary full agent with no reporting surface — which
  under D4 (fail closed) must be impossible, so this cut is a correctness question, not a
  cosmetic one;
- after enrolment, before the delegation commits: an authenticated process no coordinator may
  address;
- after the participant is live, before supervision is taken up: the forbidden state, immediately;
- backend crash after the spawn: under D5 the worker dies, but a durable record may still say it
  is live.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The interval is written with BOTH ENDS: a participant record exists from before the first
  irreversible spawn effect until either the enrolled incarnation is supervised, or the record is
  durably terminal.
- Recovery is stated for every cut above: adopt the pinned process, or terminalize it. "Started"
  is never inferred from a dispatch returning.
- A test makes an external call fail at each cut and asserts what is true on disk, in the record
  and in the process table afterwards, plus what the next start does.

title: The wave's authority model is missing: membership is not delegation, and spawn is not authorised
description:
Found by adversarial review (codex, 2026-08-24) of
.internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md, findings 7, 8, 9 and 18. It is
open question 1-4 of that document, filed as one bead because it is one topic.

The mechanism design says "addressable participant" and names none of the authority model that
is already settled elsewhere:

- D8 of the 2026-08-15 design gives a CONTROLLER SESSION — not a run, not a lineage edge — a
  REVOCABLE delegation over observe / receive-events / send-input / delegate-further / close,
  while lineage stays immutable. The mechanism design conflates membership with authority, so
  takeover, re-credentialing, a lifecycle-domain change and coordinator replacement have no
  defined effect on who may address whom. Either stale control stays live, or coordination is
  severed indiscriminately.
- D9 makes spawning a child the `delegate` effect over a resource environment, permitted only
  into an environment already in scope, with scope expansion as an escalation. ADR-0020 requires
  an immutable grant recorded on each RUN. The spawn primitive is currently described with
  neither, so the record and the API would encode the wrong principal before authority arrives.
- D13/D14 authenticate an external caller by enrolment of a process TREE, pinned by a
  non-reusable handle, approved once by a human. D5 of the mechanism design pins to the
  launcher's pid (which `exec` preserves) — necessary, and not obviously sufficient. What binds
  every LATER request to that tree, and what stops another process inside it impersonating the
  participant?
- ADR-0028 narrows by capability rather than checking before a call. One shared tool surface
  reachable by an enrolled process is the ambient dispatcher API that ADR-0028 rejects; every
  mailbox read, send, spawn, interrupt and record mutation should hold an object incapable of
  naming anything outside its delegation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four is answered in a document, and the mechanism design references the answers
  rather than restating them.
- The answer states what a wave participant may do, who granted it, what revokes it, and what a
  human takeover does to the coordinator's rights.
- Falsified if the answer is "membership implies addressability": that is the thing epic A
  enforced against, and the mechanism design must not reintroduce it.

title: Brainstorming: the orchestration mechanism — a coordinator that cannot forget it has children
description:
Continues nocx-dg51h. The owner named the pain directly: herdr and orca are CLI-shaped, the
skills shipped with them do not state a workflow, and the failure mode is that the COORDINATOR
FORGETS IT HAS CHILDREN. That is measured in this repo's own memories, not assumed:
lesson-orca-worker-waves-nocx-orchestration-check-wait (looped twice for two workers while five
were dispatched; three reports and one escalation went unread, and a false narrative reached two
commit messages), lesson-orca-worker-waves-nocx-never-leave-two (two supervisors split one queue
for 17 minutes because --wait CONSUMES), lesson-herdr-coordination-nocx-2026-08-15-in (every
background wait is reaped at the turn boundary).

nelix solves it and cannot be taken as-is, because its agents are headless: its daemon owns the
loop. Ours is an agent that exists only when it takes a turn. What DOES transfer, and is not
about headless: orchestration_id as a first-class owner-scoped record (StartLedger); ONE wait
over the N sessions of a wave via an opaque vector cursor, with an explicit empty_orchestration
marker rather than a silent spin; and router/waiters.py, which knows how many long-polls are
attached to an orchestration right now. That last one makes "there are live children and nobody
is listening" an observable backend fact rather than something an agent must remember.

Designs the mechanism for nocx-dkawo (the wave epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

A design document exists that names the mechanism by which a coordinator cannot lose track of a
live child, states what it does for BOTH callers of spec section 6 (the built-in agent, whose
loop is ours per ADR-0028, and an enrolled external CLI that we can only type into), and says
which of section 11's falsification list it accepts crossing. The owner has approved it.
notes:
SETTLED WITH THE OWNER, 2026-08-24, sections 1-3 approved before adversarial review. (1) INVARIANT: fan-out and fan-in are ONE BLOCKING CALL, so 'children started, nobody watching' is inexpressible; the harness's own subagent tool is NOT banned, because it blocks and therefore does not have this bug — herdr's does because dispatch and wait are two commands. (2) THE RECORD outlives the coordinator: participants as addressable nodes, a mailbox per participant whose read CONSUMES NOTHING, liveness with provenance bound to attempt and output offset, a WAIT-FOR GRAPH whose cycle is a PROVED deadlock (both waits are our own edges), and a listener count where zero-listeners-plus-live-children is an alarm. (3) DELIVERY: the existing internal/shellintegration detector that conservatively recognises a hand-typed ssh is extended to agent names, and the argv rewrite carries the MCP surface, hooks, and an --append-system-prompt that is where the workflow is actually stated — for EVERY participant, not only the coordinator, which is what makes a report a record and kills the self-matching sentinel. Mail piggybacks on the result of the worker's next tool call; a real interrupt stays a separate, coarser operation. TOPOLOGY: star now, participants addressable from day one; under mesh the coordinator is mirrored on MUTATIONS OF THE RECORD (file ownership, task scope, participant set), never on message content — the owner's argument, and it matches the repo's own 'trust nothing, diff everything'. INDICATOR: AD-6 binds the BACKEND, so a renderer-side indicator is legal (agent-status.ts already reads the title); evidence is split by what it may DECIDE versus what it may merely LIGHT. CROSSES KNOWINGLY: the 2026-08-15 thesis 'orchestration is a view over sessions' — its own falsification list names transactional fan-out/fan-in, and we claim the trigger has fired.
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, codex, 2026-08-24: eighteen findings, FOUR of them authorial errors in the draft. (1) 'the same seam that rewrites a hand-typed ssh' does not exist — internal/ssh/typed_wrap.go:30 keeps the user's own argv and adds two options, and the nested replacement is a backend-composed line eval'ed by the shell hook, a form ADR-0025 already refused in general. (2) That path is FAIL-OPEN by documented contract (nocx.bash:721) and fail-open is fatal for an invariant-bearing enrolment — optional integration and enrolment need opposite failure policies. (3) The 'zero cooperation' backstop does not work at all: once the agent owns the foreground, the parent shell is blocked inside that one long command and never sees what the agent spawns; requirement DROPPED, it was invented by the draft for itself. (4) The blocking call closes a MOMENT, not an interval — the very AGENTS.md rule the draft quoted at its reviewers. Replaced by a SUPERVISION LEASE. Also folded in: listener count measures connections not supervision; a wait-for cycle is a suspicion needing corroboration, not a proof; mail rides our own calls with explicit acknowledgement rather than piggybacking on arbitrary tool results; four acknowledgements never merge. Sidecar-per-participant proposed and REJECTED after costing it (descendant capture is now out of scope, process exit is already ours because nocx owns the PTY, and exec preserves the pid so D13's pin needs no live parent). Headless workers projected into panes proposed and REJECTED on the owner's constraints (subscription auth and the vendor TUI). Spec written to .internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md; unresolved findings filed as nocx-z3nkr, nocx-u0apy (children of nocx-dkawo) and nocx-cdy3v (standalone).
SECOND ADVERSARIAL PASS, codex, 2026-08-24, on the committed spec. VERDICT: the rewrite closed the repository misstatements and several false inferences, and did NOT close the central mechanism. Do not build the wave API or record before resolving: a fenced lease protocol with clock/restart/suspend semantics; delegation plus run-grant plus per-call capability identity; spawn/register/enrol/recovery transaction boundaries; the REMOTE process-tree verifier; and which acknowledgement states are facts versus declarations. THREE MORE AUTHORIAL ERRORS, same shape as the first three — citing beads from memory instead of opening them: nocx-bu6q is the INSTALLED REMOTE FOOTPRINT (manifest-owned files, generation, uninstall), not a shell alias, so the spec's claim that the alias closes it is false; nocx-8d6e is the helper-install consent ladder, not D13/D14's approval of an executable plus its descendant tree; and first-class shell integration exists only for bash and zsh (launcher_local.go:29, ReasonUnsupportedShell), so 'the panel session nocx composes' is not universal. TWO SHARPEST MECHANISM FINDINGS: (a) D3 is impossible as written — a restarted PROCESS cannot prove it held a lease, because a record naming the old holder is not a credential; fix available and already settled elsewhere, bind the lease to the controller SESSION per D8 rather than to a process. (b) The lease reintroduces POLLING, which section 12 already names as falsifying: if ordinary work does not guarantee a wave call before expiry, the coordinator must call solely to renew. Fix available: nocx owns the PTY, so coordinator death is a PROCESS FACT rather than a timeout guess, and the expiry becomes a slow backstop for the wedged/abandoned case rather than the mechanism. ALSO MISSING ENTIRELY: shell namespace collision policy (the nocxify design rejected shell-level ssh interception precisely because aliases collide, and D5 reintroduces that class); protocol version skew during live waves, made worse because D4 turns skew into total launch refusal; and THE ATTENTION QUEUE AS A DEPENDENCY — the 2026-08-15 design calls nocx-ms7v.4 load-bearing for this exact epic because 'the worker finished / is asking for you' has nowhere to go without it, and the mechanism spec left it out of its dependency set.
close_reason: Owner approved the rewritten spec on 2026-08-25, reviewing the delta in conversation: §1 (supervision is the backend's, not a lease), §4 (D1-D3 rewritten, D13 backend grid / D14 wake-by-keystroke / D15 one worker first added), §6.1 (the evidence table mapped onto internal/notify's shipped Trust instead of a second vocabulary, with the observed row left explicitly open for nocx-dkawo.4), and §7.0 (what the mechanism does for BOTH callers of the 2026-08-15 design's §6 — the acceptance criterion neither earlier revision met). Document: .internal/specs/2026-08-24-orchestration-mechanism-design.md, 528 lines, commits 3ea781fd, 0098e693, c18f1aca. Unresolved review findings remain beads rather than prose: nocx-z3nkr, nocx-u0apy under the epic, nocx-cdy3v standalone.

title: kind says what a row is; source says where it came from
description:
Found by nocx-dc2fr.7's end-to-end check, which is the only reason it was found at all.

`entries.kind` means DIFFERENT THINGS depending on the row. For a command it says WHO
submitted it (`shell` = the person, `agent` = the assistant) — decided deliberately in
design §3.1 (nocx-iadtt, nocx-e5vsc) and written into ledger_command.go in as many words:
"Author is WHO submitted the command, and it is the entry's own kind". For an assistant turn
it says WHAT the row is. And for a captured frame it says `agent` too, distinguished from a
turn only by comparing `intent` against the magic string "frame-capture".

That survived while a turn owned a `text/plain` artifact and a command owned an
`application/vt` one: the restore inferred a block's grammar from which body survived.
ADR-0037 took the turn's own artifact away — its prose moved into children — so
nocx-dc2fr.4 read the grammar from `kind` instead, which is right in principle and wrong
against a column that means two things. A command the assistant ran is `kind=agent`, so the
restore now paints it as prose with wrapping instead of a terminal grid. Live is correct;
only the restored view is broken.

Reviewed with an outside model over two rounds. Three of its objections were withdrawn under
argument, one of its corrections improved the decision, and one found an error in the
coordinator's own table. What survives is below.

Greenfield: the schema changes in place, nothing to migrate, no compatibility shims.
acceptance_criteria:
- `entries.kind` is the discriminator of WHAT A LEDGER ROW IS, and nothing else:
  `shell | ask | action | text | frame`. `agent` is renamed `ask` — the word the renderer
  already uses for this block — so nobody reads it as an author again.
- `entries.source` says WHERE THE ROW CAME FROM, closed CHECK, `user | assistant` only.
  Defined at the schema as: the IMMEDIATE subject that submitted the content or intent this
  entry represents. Initiation is NOT transitive.
- Approval does not change `source`: a call the assistant proposed stays `assistant` even
  after a person allowed it. Who proposed, who allowed, who executed and where are four
  separate facts in four separate places — asserted by a test.
- `RecordCompleted` stops writing the author into `kind`. A command the assistant ran is
  `kind='shell', source='assistant'`; one the person typed is `kind='shell', source='user'`.
- The magic string comparison `intent == "frame-capture"` is gone; a frame is `kind='frame'`,
  and its `source` comes from whoever actually asked for it — a frame the assistant's
  readScreen caused is `source='assistant'`, not `user`.
- `CHECK (parent_id IS NOT NULL OR pos IS NULL)` — a root block holds no seat. Asserted by a
  refusal test with its paired success.
- The restore draws every `kind × source` combination correctly, and the SAME matrix is
  asserted live and restored. `shell/assistant` — the case this bead exists for — is in it.
- Nothing derives authorship from `kind` any more, in Go or in the renderer. Asserted by grep
  in the report.
close_reason:
Landed in b0871af6. kind is now the discriminator of a ledger ROW — shell, ask, action, text, frame — and source says where the row came from, defined at the schema as the IMMEDIATE subject that submitted the content or intent it represents, with initiation explicitly not transitive and approval explicitly not changing it. agent became ask, the word the renderer already used. The magic-string frame check is gone. Source is REQUIRED, not defaulted, on the same reasoning that made createCommandBlock's author required: provenance the audit reads must not self-fill, and "nobody said who submitted this" must not become "the person did". Also CHECK (parent_id IS NOT NULL OR pos IS NULL), because SQLite counts NULLs as distinct and UNIQUE(parent_id,pos) never constrained roots.

The acceptance verdict is the part worth keeping. The worker's headline test for criterion 1 was VACUOUS and looked fine: blockFacts in restored-turn-order.test.ts hands the builder kind:'command', so reading the kind back off the DOM asserted what the test itself supplied. Two mutations proved it — removing the source read entirely passed, and re-pointing the grammar at the wrong column passed. The coordinator's first draft of the criterion-2 matrix had the same hole for the same reason. Both were rewritten: the defect test now lives with its owner in restore-client.test.ts asserted at restoredBody, the seam that decides, and fails under that mutation; the matrix builds its page through the real blocksForPane mapping instead of a fixture with the author pre-decided, and fails when the source read is dropped. Each states in its own words which half it proves and where the other half lives. Matrix written by the coordinator, not the worker (AGENTS.md rule 4).

Three acceptance tests in internal/app were refused by the new required-source check — the decision finding its callers, which is its purpose. They were missed because the brief excluded internal/app for its five known local-only failures (nocx-58gq, nocx-65v6); that exclusion was right for those five and wrong for a change reaching every writer. The containerised gate, which is CI, is where they surfaced. Fixed by the coordinator; internal/app is back to its baseline five.

Delivery: five omp windows, with the first agent degrading into malformed tool-call syntax and corrupting a file, and both workspaces vanishing mid-run. The worktrees survived and no work was lost. Two mechanical breaks fixed by the coordinator so a fresh agent could start from a comprehensible state: a deleted payload column, and backticks copied from a markdown brief into a Go raw string literal, which ended it. That second one is a brief-authoring lesson, not a worker error.

One container run failed TestAgentApprove_ChangedArgumentsResuspend on an i/o timeout under -race; the test passes 3/3 under -race on the host and the retried gate was clean, so it is resource contention of the nocx-2h08 class, not this change.

  that is actually done.
