description:
Epic 2 task 5. e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Drives the UI, never the store; waits on observable state, never on a duration.
- One session raises a run; the feed shows one row with a count; the spec expands it and reads the individual occurrences, each with its own time.
- Two hosts have raised; narrowing to one hides the other's rows, the panel states the narrowed count, and the bell's badge is unchanged.
- Runs on the headless path so e2e/run-in-container.sh can run it.
close_reason: e2e/notification-centre-grouping.spec.ts, green in the container on chromium across three runs, and mutation-probed: with the expandable predicate forced false the disclosure group fails, with the filter bypassed the narrowing group fails.

title: The happy path, watched end to end
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A devharness test serves a fixture OpenAPI 3.1 document over loopback, imports it BY URL, and asserts: the folder tree matches the spec tags; a chosen request has the expected method, URL and query rows; the environment carries the servers URL.
- The same test then opens that request, presses Send, and reads the response.
- It waits on observable state, never on a duration.
- It runs with the disposable `$HOME` the suite requires.

title: The import dialog takes a file, a paste or a URL
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A person can reach the OpenAPI import from the collections tree without editing any file.
- The dialog offers all three sources; choosing URL reveals the connection picker beside the URL field, listing global connections plus a direct option.
- The destination folder field has a Browse button using the same `dialog.*` method the Postman import already uses.
- Only kit components: the guard against raw controls and direct Kobalte imports stays green, and the surface adds no `background`, `border`, `color`, `font-*`, `padding` or `box-shadow` to a kit component.
- After an import, the `Unsupported` list is shown, as it already is for Postman.
- The test drives the seam a person reaches: the control exists, is enabled from the state a user starts in, and activating it reaches the client method.

title: api.import.openapi, with its contract
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- One new JSON-RPC method `api.import.openapi` taking the source (file | text | url), the optional connection id, and the destination; returning the `Unsupported` list in the shape `api.import.postman` already uses.
- `contracts/api.import.openapi.json` lands in the SAME commit, with `additionalProperties: false` and an explicit `required`.
- `npm run contracts:check` passes with the generated renderer type committed.
- `…_DTOConformsToContract` and `…_OverTheWireConformsToContract` both exist; the second validates the real result off the real socket, not a payload the test built.
- No `Unsupported` entry on the wire carries a value out of the document.

title: The spec is fetched by a send, through a connection the person chose
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `capability.ImportOpenAPI` takes a source of file | text | url and, for url, sends a GET through `internal/apisend` with `RouteID` = the chosen connection. There is NO second HTTP client: assert `internal/capability` gains no `net/http.Client` construction for this path.
- The fetch completes BEFORE `ImportInto` is called: on a fetch that 404s, times out, exceeds the byte ceiling, or returns a non-spec, `dest` does not exist afterwards. One test per failure.
- The fetch sends no credential. A 401 surfaces as an error naming the status and telling the person to download the document and import it as a file — visible in the product, not only in a log.
- `internal/apiimport` still cannot reach `net/http`: `TestPackageNeverExecs` unchanged and green.
- The `http://` rule is not re-derived: the path goes through `httppolicy` via `apisend`.

title: ImportInto recognises a third document shape and writes the tree
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- `ImportInto` dispatches to the OpenAPI converter on the top-level `openapi` key, and to the Postman converter on `item`/`info.schema`. A document with neither is refused by name. Assert both JSON shapes route correctly — they share a first byte.
- The whole tree lands as ONE atomic arrival: `dest` does not exist until every file is written, synced and renamed.
- An FS failure injected on the Nth file leaves `dest` absent — no partial collection.
- An existing `dest` is refused, never replaced.
- The converter is reachable from `main`: `deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive <converter symbol> ./...` prints a path from `main`, not "reachable only through reflection".

title: servers becomes one environment, and the servers we did not take are said out loud
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- Exactly one environment file is written. For a URL import it is built from the server whose origin matches the fetched URL; for file/text it is `servers[0]`.
- It carries `baseUrl` and the route the person chose (`RouteConnection` + profile id, or `RouteDirect`).
- A server URL with variables (`https://{region}.api.com`) is filled from each variable's `default`.
- Every other `servers` entry produces an `Unsupported` line naming that server. No environment is created for it — asserted by counting environment files, so a future "helpful" addition fails this test.
- Variable names from `securitySchemes` appear in the environment's `SecretVars`; no values do.

title: An operation becomes a request
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- One operation produces one `apicoll.Request`; folder = first `tag` minted by `slug()`; untagged lands in the root.
- Name = `summary`, else `operationId`, else `METHOD /path`. A name of `../../etc` yields a folder segment `etc` and no traversal — assert against the minted PATH, not the display name.
- URL is `{{baseUrl}}` + path, and `/users/{id}` becomes `/users/{{id}}`.
- Path parameters land in `Request.Variables` (the request's own, not the environment), empty and enabled.
- Query parameters land in `Query`: `required: true` → `Enabled: true`, otherwise present with `Enabled: false`.
- Header parameters land in `Headers`.
- A `requestBody` with an `example` carries it VERBATIM plus the media type as `Content-Type`; without one the body is empty. No body is ever generated from a schema.
- Auth: `http`+`bearer` → `Auth{Kind: bearer, Var: "{{<scheme key>}}"}`; `http`+`basic` → basic; `apiKey` → apikey carrying its name and `in`; `oauth2`/`openIdConnect` → `AuthNone` + an `Unsupported` line. Operation-level `security` wins over the document's.
- No file written anywhere under the collection root names a secret (design §8); `BindWriter` receives ZERO calls on this path.

title: The OpenAPI document parses, and a version we cannot do is refused by name
description:
## Acceptance Criteria

- A 3.0 and a 3.1 fixture both parse into the document model; JSON and YAML spellings of the same fixture produce an identical model (yaml.v3 is already a direct dependency — no new one).
- A document with `swagger: "2.0"` is refused with an error naming Swagger 2.0 and naming 3.0/3.1 as what is supported. It is NOT parsed as far as it will go.
- Every bound is a number and each has a test that crosses it: document bytes, operation count (reuse `names.go` `maxItems`), internal `$ref` depth.
- An internal `$ref` resolves; a cyclic one stops at the depth bound and does not recurse.
- An external `$ref` (one naming another URL) is NEVER fetched: the package still cannot reach `net/http` (`TestPackageNeverExecs` stays green) and the ref becomes an `Unsupported` entry naming the operation.
- No `Unsupported.What` ever carries a value out of the document.

title: [epic] A collection is made from the service's own OpenAPI document, fetched from wherever it lives
acceptance_criteria:
DONE WHEN a person gives the import dialog the OpenAPI URL of a service reachable only through an SSH connection, picks that connection, and receives a collection whose folders are the spec tags, whose requests are its operations, and whose one environment already carries the servers URL and that same connection — then opens a request and presses Send having edited nothing but a value. Watched end to end by a devharness test that serves a fixture OpenAPI 3.1 document over loopback.

Deliberately out: bodies generated from schemas, Swagger 2.0, external $ref fetching, OAuth2 flows, re-import/sync of a changed spec, authenticating the spec fetch.

title: A feed row stops being clickable the moment its session ends
description:
`PaneManager.findBySession` (frontend/src/panes.ts:1979) resolves through `content.activeOrigin()`, which returns null once the terminal content has seen its session exit (frontend/src/terminal-content.ts:713). So a `session.ended` row -- the epic's own first source -- is unactivatable by construction, even when its tab is still on the strip marked as lost. The epic promises "clicking the row focuses the tab".

Second half of the same gap: `notify.raise` leaves `Attribution.Backend` empty (internal/transport/ws_notify.go:150-158) while `findBySession` requires 'local', so a program notification from a live tab is unactivatable too.

Found by the epic's e2e check (2026-08-22), which fails on this assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A pane is resolvable by the session id it holds for as long as the pane exists, whether or not that session has ended -- the lookup does not go through the live content origin.
- `notify.raise` stamps `Attribution.Backend` with the local route, so a program notification's row resolves too.
- `canActivate` then means what the panel's meta line claims: the row is inert exactly when the tab is gone, not when the shell exited.
- A test drives it through the UI: a row from a tab that is still open focuses that tab; a row whose tab has been closed is inert.
close_reason: Closed

title: A local shell that exits cleanly is reported as a lost connection
description:
`lifecyclePTY` (internal/app/app.go:1511) embeds the `pty.Pty` INTERFACE, and `WaitErr() (error, bool)` is declared only on the concrete `*LocalPty` (internal/pty/pty_local.go:277). A method on a concrete type is not promoted through an embedded interface, so the type assertion in internal/session/session.go:905 fails for every enhanced local session, `ExitOutcome` has no shell report to read, and it correctly refuses to invent one -- returning ExitInterrupted.

User-visible: a local shell you exit normally leaves its tab marked "Connection lost" instead of closing, and the exit status is gone. Predates the notification centre; found by that epic's e2e check (2026-08-22), which needs the exited/interrupted distinction to map notification levels.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `*lifecyclePTY` satisfies `interface{ WaitErr() (error, bool) }` by forwarding to the embedded pty when that pty provides it, and reports `false` when it does not.
- A test asserts an enhanced local session whose shell exits 0 classifies as ExitExited with status 0, and one that exits non-zero carries that status -- not ExitInterrupted.
- The paired failure test: a session whose pty genuinely provides no report still classifies as ExitInterrupted and does not panic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Every activity-bar panel invents its own arrangement inside a shell that is already shared
description:
Owner: bring every activity-bar panel to one shape. The shell is shared and applied centrally (sidebar.tsx constructs SidebarView once for every view), but each panel invented its own arrangement inside it, and the differences only surface when somebody looks at two panels in one session.

Known so far, from fixing Files: the filter slot existed with ZERO callers so every panel rendered its search field in the scrolling body and every filter scrolled away; .files-filter carried horizontal margin on top of the body's own inset, leaving the field 48px narrower than its panel; and .ui-sidebar-view__header > h2 set only flex, so the heading kept the UA's 1.5em and 0.83em margins and the header measured 72px for one word. Files is fixed and is the reference; Ports, Git and Notes are not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every panel's filter is declared through SidebarViewDescriptor.filter and pinned by the shell; none renders a search field inside the scrolling body.
- No panel adds horizontal inset on top of the body's own; content across panels lines up.
- Panels that do not go through SidebarView are found and either moved onto it or the reason recorded.
- Differences between panels are enumerated in the report — what each was doing and why it is now one thing — rather than silently normalised.
- Kit-level where the kit can own it; a panel says only what the kit cannot know for itself.
close_reason: Merged as c955ddb3..ddcf7c82 plus the coordinator's two follow-ups. Three panels moved onto the shell's pinned filter slot (Ports, Git, Notes); Files was already there. THE DELIVERABLE IS THE TEST, not the diff: panels-one-shape.test.ts reads the SHIPPED stylesheets, because jsdom computes no cascade, and binds three rules for panels nobody has written yet — header, filter and body share one inset; no panel root adds its own; .ui-sidebar-view__body is the one scroll owner. The worker named the two divergences it could not touch (they were in another worker's branch) instead of working around them, and recorded ops-list as an exception ON THE RECORD rather than excluding it silently. Both closed once that branch landed: the Files filter's own margin is gone now the kit row supplies it, the operations headings no longer inset 16px on top of the body's 8px, and its two lists no longer each declare a scroller inside the scrolling body. The exception list is back to empty, which is the correct lifetime for it.

title: Decide how much of a collapsed run the feed keeps
description:
Epic 1 collapses a consecutive run into one row: Count rises, the newest Event replaces the held one, and the constituent occurrences are gone. Epic 2's success criterion is that a collapsed row EXPANDS to the individual occurrences, each keeping its own timestamp and unread mark -- which the epic-1 shape cannot serve.

Retaining all constituents is not the answer either: the flood test admits 10000 occurrences from one session, and keeping them restores exactly the unbounded growth collapse exists to prevent. So the question is what bounded remainder an expansion is allowed to show, and how the row states honestly what it is no longer showing.

Found by review of the epic-1 backend (codex, 2026-08-22), not by a user.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A decision is recorded (ADR or a spec section) naming: what a collapsed row retains per constituent, the bound on that retention, what an expansion shows when the bound was hit, and where the retained data lives (the Occurrence, or beside it).
- The bound is stated in both currencies the feed already uses -- a count and bytes -- or the decision says explicitly why one suffices.
- The decision names what happens to a constituent's unread mark when the run collapses, given that epic 1 clears the row's ReadAt on every join.
close_reason: Decided in .internal/plans/2026-08-22-notification-centre-epic-2.md D2: a row retains its newest MaxRunRetained (20) constituents as RunMember{ID,At,Title,ReadAt}, counts the rest in RunDropped, member bytes count against MaxRetainedBytes, and MarkAllRead marks the row and every retained member while a later join clears only the row's mark.

title: A queued file exists only in a loop variable, so a multi-file drop shows one file and hides the rest
description:
Owner dropped two files: one uploads and the second is nowhere. Not a display bug — the queue does not exist as data.

upload-flow.ts sends strictly one at a time (for … await sendOne(…)), and the store only learns of a transfer when files.upload has returned its transferId. So a file waiting its turn lives in a loop variable and nowhere else: it cannot be shown, counted or cancelled. Drop five and you see one, with no way to know how many are coming or to stop them.

The sequential send itself is deliberate (design section 4, one at a time per binding) and stays. What is missing is that the batch is not represented.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Drop two files on a tab. The first shows in Operations with progress; the second appears only when the first finishes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The whole batch is registered before the first send, so every file is visible from the moment it is dropped.
- A waiting file says it is waiting rather than showing a progress bar at zero, which would claim bytes are moving.
- Cancelling a waiting file removes it from the batch and sends NOTHING on the wire — there is no transfer to cancel yet.
- Cancelling a waiting file does not cancel the batch, and cancelling the running one does not silently drop the rest — say which it does and test it.
- The badge counts what a person would call outstanding, and the grouping in the list still reads correctly with waiting rows in it.
- A refusal that stops the batch (an unusable destination) accounts for the files never attempted rather than leaving them waiting forever.
close_reason: Merged as 07f52646 + caa7d13a. 3879 tests. THE QUEUE: the whole batch is registered before the first send, so every dropped file is visible, counted and stoppable from the moment it lands; a waiting row says it is waiting and draws no bar at zero, which would have claimed bytes were moving. Cancelling a waiting file sends nothing on the wire — there is no transfer yet — asserted on the service double rather than by eye. THE FOLDER: refused in the drop handler before anything is registered, via webkitGetAsEntry().isDirectory off dataTransfer.items, with tests asserting it is NOT decided by size or MIME type; a mixed drop sends the files, names the folder and says how many are on their way. THE MANGLED NAME WAS NOT OURS, and the worker proved it rather than assuming: File.name is passed verbatim in the browser and filepath.Base in Go, nothing anywhere composes a name; the Wails half already refused directories via !info.Mode().IsRegular(), which is how it established the owner was on the browser path, and 192 B is an APFS directory entry. It could not reproduce 15498198pril and says so — then left a test that feeds exactly that string in as a File.name and requires the same characters out, so a composer introduced later fails rather than being argued about.

title: The operations row is hard to read: no hierarchy, wrapping numbers, a hairline progress bar and a button eating the width
description:
Owner, looking at a running upload in the panel: everything is too small and hard to take in. Named concretely rather than as a feeling.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a large upload and open the Operations view at the panel's default width.
2. The progress bar is a hairline between the title and the numbers; '99.1 MB of 328.3 MB' and '7.1 MB/s' wrap onto two lines; the path shows as /home/... ; Cancel takes about a third of the width.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Progress is the visual anchor of a running row, not a hairline between two text blocks.
- A percentage is shown, so nobody does arithmetic to learn that 99.1 of 328.3 is a third.
- Nothing wraps, and the row's height does not change as the numbers do.
- Cancel stops competing with the content for width, while staying keyboard reachable and discoverable without hover-only knowledge.
- A path ellipsises so the LEAF survives — the tail is the informative end.
- A finished row and a running row are distinguishable at a glance rather than by reading.
- Checked at the panel's MINIMUM width and at a wide one; the kit is used and never repainted.

title: An open is answered before it is finished, and nothing can wait for the difference
description:
Named by the worker that fixed nocx-bmpif, which closed the reads rather than the window. An open is not over when its RESPONSE arrives — the subscriber install and other tail work continue after it — and no test helper can wait for that tail. Every wait built on 'the response came back, therefore the server is ready' is racy by construction, and the two defects fixed today were both symptoms of it.

The worker names two candidate shapes: a signal the helper can wait on, or the integrationPTYFactory pattern generalised. It did not choose between them and neither do I.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A caller, test or otherwise, can wait for an open to be COMPLETE rather than merely answered.
- The waits fixed in nocx-bmpif and 1ab22b28 are re-expressed on it, so the workaround does not outlive its cause.
- The fix is argued against the alternative rather than picked.

title: The bell, the panel, and click-to-tab
description:
Plan task 8. BellIcon in the kit, notifications-panel.tsx, sidebar badgeCount, registration in main.tsx.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The bell is a view in the top zone of the activity bar, not an action.
- With zero unread the bell carries NO badge element at all.
- Rows are kit RecordRow inside a role=list; kind badge toned from level; count > 1 renders as xN.
- The panel header action is an IconButton "Mark all read", disabled at zero unread.
- An empty feed renders the kit EmptyState.
- dropped.count > 0 renders one non-activatable row at the bottom naming the count and the span.
- Activating a row resolves (backendId, sessionId) to a tab in the RENDERER and focuses it; a row whose session is gone is not activatable and says so.
- No CSS in notifications-panel.css sets background, border, color, font-*, padding or box-shadow on a ui-* class.
- A test asserts the unread count is unchanged after focusing the tab a notification came from, and changes only on Mark all read.
close_reason: Closed

title: The wire: three methods, three schemas, both conformance tests
description:
Plan task 5. contracts/notify.feed.{read,markRead,changed}.schema.json, generated renderer types, internal/transport/ws_notify_feed.go, BroadcastFeedChanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- notify.feed.read returns {revision, unreadCount, occurrences[], dropped} and nothing else; additionalProperties:false on every object.
- Each occurrence carries id, at, title, body, kind, level, count, read, backendId, sessionId, host and NO trust.
- notify.feed.markRead returns {revision}; notify.feed.changed carries {revision} and nothing else.
- With no feed wired all three answer -32601.
- npm run contracts:check passes; a _DTOConformsToContract and an _OverTheWireConformsToContract case exist for each method.
- BroadcastFeedChanged reaches every client and survives a full queue on one of them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ingress: stamping moves, once
description:
Plan task 3. Create internal/notify/ingress.go; Router.Raise stops stamping At; Attribution gains Backend.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Admit stamps ev.At from the injected clock when zero and leaves a non-zero At alone.
- Router.Raise no longer stamps At and its comment says why.
- Admit records into the feed BEFORE submitting for delivery.
- An event whose policy disposition is DispositionSuppressed is still in the feed.
- Attribution.Backend is carried through unchanged and reaches the feed.
- Failure-path tests: sink refuses, feed full (both Admits still deliver), MarkAllRead racing Admit under -race, occurrence interval has both ends.
close_reason: Closed

title: session.ended, the feed's first honest source
description:
Plan task 4. Raise a session.ended event from monitorExit in internal/transport/ws.go; add the route in internal/app/app.go.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Exactly one session.ended event per session end, with Trust: TrustAttested.
- Level maps from cause: ExitExited status 0 -> success; non-zero -> warning; ExitInterrupted -> warning.
- Title names host and cause; body carries the exit status when there is one; neither is built from any byte of the stream (AD-6).
- Attribution carries Backend "local", the session id and the host.
- A server with no ingress wired still emits the exit notification and does not panic.
close_reason: Closed

title: Wire it at the composition root
description:
Plan task 6. Construct the feed and ingress in internal/app/app.go, bind OnChange to the transport broadcast.

## Acceptance Criteria
- notifyFeed is constructed with explicit limits and its OnChange is bound to the transport's broadcast.
- transport.WithNotifyRaiser receives the INGRESS, not the policy.
- transport.WithNotifyFeed receives the feed.
- deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive on internal/notify.(*Feed).Add prints a path from main, not "reachable only through reflection".
close_reason: Closed

title: The renderer's client and feed store
description:
Plan task 7. frontend/src/notify/feed-client.ts, feed-store.ts, feed-store.test.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On creation the store fetches a snapshot and subscribes to notify.feed.changed.
- A hint at or below the store's own revision is ignored.
- A burst of hints coalesces into exactly one in-flight refetch.
- markRead() applies the revision from the method result directly; a later changed for that revision is a no-op.
- destroy() unsubscribes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Flood collapse
description:
Plan task 2. CollapseKey{Backend,Session,Kind,Level} plus FeedLimits.CollapseWindow; consecutive repeats compact into one row.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Consecutive Adds sharing a CollapseKey inside CollapseWindow of the previous LastAt compact: Count rises, LastAt and Event become the newest, no new id minted.
- A matching key arriving after the window opens a new occurrence with a new id.
- A key differing in ANY component, including Level, never collapses.
- Collapsing into a read occurrence marks it unread again.
- Flood property test: 10000 occurrences from one session leave the feed inside MaxOccurrences AND leave a pre-existing unread danger row from another session present.
close_reason: Closed

title: The acceptance check
description:
Plan task 9. e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The spec drives the UI, not the store: clicks the bell, reads rendered rows, clicks Mark all read.
- It waits on observable state, never on a duration.
- It runs on the headless path (cmd/devharness + vite) so it works in e2e/run-in-container.sh.
- After mark-read the badge element is gone and the row is still present.
close_reason: Closed

title: The occurrence record and the bounded feed
description:
Plan task 1. Create internal/notify/feed.go + feed_test.go: Occurrence, FeedLimits, NewFeed, Add, Snapshot, MarkAllRead, OnChange, DroppedRecord.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Add returns a distinct id per call; Snapshot lists occurrences newest first.
- Exceeding MaxOccurrences evicts the oldest READ occurrence first; an unread one only when no read one exists.
- Exceeding MaxRetainedBytes (UTF-8 Title+Body of every held occurrence) evicts by the same rule until inside budget.
- Every eviction increments Dropped.Count and widens [Oldest, Newest]; the dropped record is outside the occurrence budget and never itself evicted.
- Revision is monotonic and bumps on Add, on MarkAllRead and on an eviction.
- MarkAllRead sets ReadAt on every unread occurrence and returns the new revision.
- OnChange fires after the mutation is visible to Snapshot, never before.
close_reason: Closed

title: A contract test was passing because the old readers ate the frames it did not want
description:
Surfaced by the inbox fix (07bb5522, nocx-hbdw4.2) and caused by it in the honest sense: the test was passing because the old frame-eating readers threw away the early notifications it did not want.

The shared reader lives in ws_test.go, which ws_contract_test.go uses without having been edited. The inbox now delivers the FIRST matching notification instead of whatever survived being eaten, and the first session.integrationChanged in this sequence is 'starting' with no reason yet. The test wants the OUTCOME, which is a later frame.

So the test asked for 'a session.integrationChanged' and meant 'the one that says how it ended'. That distinction did not exist while frames were being dropped.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. ./scripts/ci-linux.sh: --- FAIL TestSessionIntegrationChanged_BootstrapOutcomesAreReadableOffTheWire/no_hasher_on_the_far_host, ws_contract_test.go:5583: status = starting, want conventional.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The test waits for the outcome frame rather than the first frame, and says in its own words which it wants.
- It still fails when the backend genuinely does not report the outcome — prove it by suppressing that, not by watching it stay green.
- Any sibling test in the same file relying on the same accident is found and fixed with it; do not fix one and leave the rest to surface one ci-linux run at a time.
close_reason: Merged as 3be17f9e + 1ab22b28. 43 waits examined. A wait for a notification now names the frame it means by a property rather than by position, so it does not break the day a third frame is emitted. Proven by suppression, not inspection. A SECOND defect was found and committed separately: openSSHOverSocket never waited for the subscriber install, so a test captured a nil subscriber, put it back and read that as a product defect — fixed by giving that opener the wait openSessionOnConn has had all along, across 12 call sites.

title: Restore knows only one kind of entry: the agent's attribution and every dialogue are lost
acceptance_criteria:
A restored tab shows what the pane actually held: shell commands as command blocks with their
author, and the assistant's questions and answers as the dialogue blocks they were.

## What the owner saw, 2026-08-22

"После восстановления вкладки вся атрибуция, что эта команда была запущена агентом, и все
диалоги пропали. Они должны быть обычными блоками."

## Cause — three, and they compound

Measured in the code, not guessed:

1. **The author is dropped.** `restoredBlock()` calls `createCommandBlock(...)` WITHOUT its
   `author` argument (frontend/src/scrollback/restored-block.ts), so it defaults to 'shell' and
   the `agent` badge cannot be painted. `RestoredBlockFacts` has no author field at all, and
   `blocksForPane` never asks for one.
2. **Every entry kind becomes a command block.** `ledger.query` carries a `kind` filter of
   shell | agent | action and `blocksForPane` sends none, so agent questions and tool actions
   come back too — and are mapped into `RestorableBlock` with `command: e.intent` and drawn
   through the command path. A question to the assistant is restored as a command whose text is
   the question.
3. **The answer cannot be drawn even when its entry is there.** `bodyForBlock` takes only the
   `application/vt` artifact; an agent answer's artifact is written `text/plain`
   (internal/content/ledger_agent_sqlite.go). So the body resolves to null and the block says
   "Output is no longer kept" — the sentence for an evicted body, about an answer that is
   sitting in the ledger.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something, and run a command through it, in a pane.
2. Restore the tab.
3. The agent badge is gone from the command; the dialogue is a command block with no output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **`author` becomes a REQUIRED parameter of createCommandBlock** — the owner asked for this
  by name. Not optional with a default: a call site that forgets it must not compile. This is
  the same class of defect as the `close` wrapper that silently dropped `model` (a18cead9) —
  an arity the type system was happy to accept. Assert the badge on a restored agent command.
- The restore path knows what kind each entry is and draws it as that kind: a shell command as
  a command block, an assistant turn as the dialogue it was. Decide deliberately what a
  kind=action entry becomes — the tool-call line has an owner in the answer flow now
  (nocx-shxv0), so an action restored as a top-level command block would be a second owner.
  State the decision in the code.
- An answer's body is drawn from the artifact it actually has. "Output is no longer kept" is
  reserved for a body that is genuinely evicted (ADR-0019 §7) — a sentence that lies about
  retention is worse than a blank.
- Asserted end to end: a pane with a command, an agent command and a dialogue is restored and
  all three come back as themselves.
notes:
Question closed before the work started, 2026-08-22: what a kind=action entry becomes on restore is ALREADY decided, in frontend/src/command-ledger.ts — 'a third kind and can never be an author: an action has no block and no command line'. So an action is not restored as a block at all; only shell entries and agent turns are. A command the assistant ran is an ORDINARY shell entry with author='agent' (terminal-content.ts submitAgentCommand -> submitShellCommand -> ledger.open(..., author)), so it already comes back as a command block and needs only its badge. Do not re-decide this in the bead.

--- Cause corrected and shape decided with the owner, 2026-08-22 ---

THE BEAD'S CAUSE 2 IS WRONG, measured rather than read. Dialogues do not come
back mis-rendered; they do not come back AT ALL. SubmitAgentAsk writes the
question and the answer with session_id and NO pane_id
(ledger_agent_sqlite.go:486 and :552), and the restore read is `pane_id = ?`.
A session is gone by the time a restore runs (D5), so the dialogue is anchored
to the one thing that cannot survive. Proof, red today:
internal/content/ledger_pane_anchor_test.go
TestADialogueIsFoundByItsPaneAfterARestart -> the page is [].

Nobody decided the session anchor. The entries table has two writers: Submit
(commands) and SubmitAgentAsk (dialogues). The pane-as-durable-anchor decision
(nocx-rtg0.28, design §6.1) reached the first and never the second — the
assistant design's own minimum subset says entries carry "session and
environment", and the pane never entered its input. Two writers of one table
drifted, and each is correct about what it was told.

THE SHAPE, owner 2026-08-22, on being shown the above: "вопрос - это команда.
А ответ - вывод. Зачем что-то изобретать?"

1. ONE ENTRY PER TURN. The answer stops being its own entry and becomes the
   BODY of the question entry — exactly what a command's output is to a
   command. This supersedes the assistant design §5 ("the answer — an entry of
   kind = agent, joined to the question by a caused-by edge"). §5's stated
   reason survives untouched: it is about the answer's body being an ARTIFACT
   with provenance rather than a string in a column, which is what it stays.
   Nothing depended on the second entry beyond its id being a ROUTING ADDRESS
   for deltas, reasoning, tool-call lines and copy — the question's id serves
   all four.
2. THE TURN CARRIES THE PANE, like every other block. This is the defect.
   There is nothing to derive it from server-side: sessions know only their
   workspace, so the renderer sends it, exactly as ledger.open already does.
3. NO NEW FIELD, NO ROLE, NO AUTHOR/KIND SPLIT. The restore path picks the
   block's grammar from what the body IS, which is stored and never inferred:
   a command's terminal body is application/vt and its plain copy is marked
   derived_from it; an assistant turn's text/plain body is the original and no
   vt body ever exists for it. So: has a terminal body -> command block (with
   the agent badge from the author field); has none -> ask block, prose
   grammar. Considered and rejected as unnecessary: a stored `role` column,
   a backend-derived role, and splitting author from kind.
4. TOOL CALLS STAY THEIR OWN ENTRIES and stay non-blocks. But they are
   currently anchored to NOTHING — internal/assistant/policy.go:977 and :1074
   Submit a kind=action entry with no pane, no session, no conversation and no
   edge. So a restored turn cannot know which calls were its own, and would
   come back as bare prose without what the assistant DID (which nocx-shxv0
   made visible on purpose). Link the action to its turn with the relation the
   store already has: caused-by, which the collapse in (1) frees up — it is
   what joins the answer to the question today.
5. REASONING IS NOT PERSISTED, and the owner decided it stays that way. It is
   several times longer than the answer, closed by default, and most people
   never open it. A restored turn therefore has NO reasoning note at all —
   absent, never an empty one, and the expandReasoning setting must not
   contradict that. Filed separately if it is ever wanted.
close_reason: Shipped in 565c3be7 (the fix + ADR-0036) and ee90a03b (the end-to-end check). A turn is one entry: kind=agent, question as intent, answer as an artifact on its own run; agent.ask answers with entryId and the four contracts moved with it. The transport anchors the turn to its pane (ws_agent.go in.PaneID = panePtr(sess.PaneID())), which is the half that made dialogues absent rather than mis-drawn. Restore reads the grammar from the body the entry HAS — application/vt means command, a text/plain original means turn — so no role column, no backend-derived role, no author/kind split; that last stays filed as nocx-69x9e. author is now a REQUIRED parameter of createCommandBlock. Actions stay out of the restore entirely. e2e/agent-restore.spec.ts drives a person's command, an assistant command through the run tool (the first e2e to drive run at all) and a dialogue through one restart, and was verified against three mutations, one per claim.

title: The answer is painted as plain text: no markdown, no syntax highlighting
acceptance_criteria:
An answer that contains code reads as code, and an answer with structure reads as structure.

## Why

Owner, 2026-08-22, refusing to accept the assistant surface as shipped: "нужна подсветка
синтаксиса ответа и кода (если они есть)."

Today the answer block renders the model's prose as terminal rows. The renderer ALREADY has
the two things this needs and they must not be rebuilt: shell-highlight.ts (the same lexer the
command editor and the frozen block header use) and the fenced-code handling the answer flow
does when it splits ``` regions into their own container (scrollback/blocks.ts).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fenced code block in an answer is highlighted. Where the language is a shell, it goes
  through the EXISTING lexer — one owner of "what does shell look like" (AGENTS.md). Where it
  is another language, the bead decides and states what happens: a deliberate plain rendering
  is an acceptable answer, a second shell highlighter is not.
- Markdown structure a model actually emits is rendered: headings, lists, inline code, bold.
  Say in the code what is deliberately NOT rendered and why.
- The model's text is DATA, never markup: whatever renders it escapes every byte. The frozen
  header path already innerHTMLs a string the lexer escaped — follow that shape and assert the
  escaping with a test that feeds the answer a tag.
- An answer with no code and no structure renders exactly as it does today.
- Nothing here may repaint the kit (AGENTS.md): a surface places, it does not restyle.
close_reason: Shipped in 789d55f6 on feat/ai-assistant; unit tests + typecheck + pre-commit gates (incl. containerized go -race and vitest) green.

title: Thinking is collapsed with no way to keep it open
acceptance_criteria:
A person who wants to watch the model think can say so once, in Settings, and every answer
opens its reasoning from then on.

## Why

nocx-s92so put reasoning in its own collapsed note — right for a person who does not want it,
wrong for the owner, who does: "Нужна настройка позволяющая отображать thinking раскрытым
всегда." Raised while refusing to accept the surface as shipped.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A setting in Settings, in the kit's own vocabulary (Checkbox variant="switch" — read
  frontend/src/ui/README.md before building anything), that makes the reasoning note render
  open. Default stays closed: it is the answer a person came for, not the thinking.
- It applies to answers that arrive AFTER it is set and to ones already on screen — a setting
  the surface contradicts is the defect ("a soft degrade must be visible in the product").
- The person can still collapse an individual note with the setting on; the setting is the
  default, not a lock.
- A model with no reasoning renders nothing at all, with the setting on or off.
- It goes through the settings document the way every other setting does (ADR-0033: UI state
  is a document, not a setting) — do not invent a second store.

title: The tool-call line shows a session UUID, which means nothing to the person
acceptance_criteria:
The line naming what the assistant did is readable by a person: it says WHICH pane, in the
words the product already uses for panes, never a 32-character id.

## What happens

Owner, 2026-08-22, reviewing the shipped nocx-shxv0 surface and REFUSING TO ACCEPT IT:

    readScreen   9bb9a7602c27e8ba0741972c7049b54b
    blocks.list  9bb9a7602c27e8ba0741972c7049b54b
    blocks.read  9bb9a7602c27e8ba0741972c7049b54b
    run          9bb9a7602c27e8ba0741972c7049b54b

"А вот эта цифра пользователю ни о чем не говорит."

## Cause, and why it is not simply a bug

It is the deliberate design working as specified, and the specification being wrong for one
resource kind. contracts/agent.runToolCall.schema.json sends the DERIVED resource rather than
the raw arguments — right, and for a good reason (one derivation, shared with the approval
prompt). But for kind=session the derived resource IS the session id, and a session id is an
internal handle, not a word about the world.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant anything that makes it call readScreen or a blocks tool.
2. The tool-call line in the answer names the tool and a 32-hex session id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A session resource renders as the pane's own name — the same words the tab and the chip
  already use (the cwd/host label, e.g. "home/dev") — never the id. Asserted.
- ONE owner for "what is this session called to a person". The tab strip and the chip already
  derive it; use that derivation rather than writing a second (AGENTS.md).
- The id does not vanish from the WIRE — the renderer routes and dedupes on it. This is about
  what is painted.
- A path resource is unchanged: a path is already the person's own word for the thing.
- The approval prompt gets the same treatment, or this bead says why not — the two surfaces
  show the same derived resource.
close_reason: Shipped in 789d55f6 on feat/ai-assistant; unit tests + typecheck + pre-commit gates (incl. containerized go -race and vitest) green.

title: Compaction: the rolling summary, the summarizing role, defrag, and the failure path
acceptance_criteria:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md §3. Order-of-work item 6.
Blocked by the window task (nothing to trigger on) and the conversation task (nothing to fold).

## What a person gets

They work for an hour and the conversation stays inside the model's window with no action from
them. Nobody is ever asked to compact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The trigger is the estimated prompt exceeding a fraction of the window, with a reserve for the
  answer. Then, and only then, the middle is folded.
- PROTECTED, asserted: the system prompt (rebuilt, never summarized), the newest turns up to a
  token budget, and EVERY question the person typed, anywhere in the range, verbatim.
- FOLDED: answers and tool traces older than the tail, into ONE rolling summary — a durable
  ledger entry with an edge to what it absorbed, so restore needs no special case. Marked in the
  message itself as reference and not as a task.
- The summarizer is a third ModelRole (summarizing), resolved through the roles surface exactly
  as answering is. Unassigned falls back to the answering role's endpoint WITH A NOTE in the UI,
  never silently — it costs money the person did not ask to spend.
- Defrag: when the rolling summary exceeds its own threshold, one call re-summarizes it in place.
- The failure path, asserted: the answer is NEVER blocked. The turn proceeds with the tail alone
  plus an honest marker that older turns could not be summarized, the failure is recorded on the
  run, and three consecutive failures over the same range drop it rather than retrying forever.
- Micro-compaction is deliberately out.

title: The conversation is assembled from the ledger, and clear ends it
acceptance_criteria:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md §2. Order-of-work item 5.
This is the one the owner asked for: today a follow-up cannot mean what it says.

## What a person gets

They ask a question, then a follow-up with nothing attached, and the answer is about the same
thing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new ask assembles, from the ledger's entries FOR THIS PANE, in order: every question entry
  verbatim as user, every answer artifact as assistant, and for a turn that used tools ONE
  short factual line and never the output — what was called, how it ended, how big the result
  was ("ran ls -a → 12 lines", "refused by policy").
- The tool line is DERIVED FROM THE LEDGER, never written by the answering model. It is the
  cheapest thing in the transcript and the first to become fiction otherwise (design, Risks).
- The full text stays where it is — the ledger artifact the attempt wrote — and the model
  reaches it with the block tools that already exist (nocx-5u3oz.6). Two ways to fetch a stored
  result would be two ways to get them out of step.
- References stay attached to the turn they were attached in: a frame's text is sent in the
  turn the person attached it and is not re-sent afterwards.
- The range is SINCE THE LAST CLEAR. clear already takes the blocks and the chips; it takes the
  conversation with them, and it is the only gesture that does.
- Asserted end to end: a question, then a follow-up naming nothing, and the answer is about the
  first thing. Watched through the real seam, not by reading the assembler's return value.

title: The window is fetched per (endpoint, model) and shown as a percentage
acceptance_criteria:
Design .internal/specs/2026-08-21-what-the-model-is-told-design.md §3a and the measure half of
§3. Order-of-work item 4. It blocks the compaction task, because a fold cannot be triggered by
a number nobody computes.

## What a person gets

The pane says how much of the model's context is in use, as a percentage of a window that was
FETCHED rather than assumed — and says "estimate" while the number behind it is one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The window size is captured per (endpoint, model) where the provider reports it: OpenRouter's
  /models carries context_length, and the endpoint editor already reads that endpoint for model
  discovery — extend that read rather than adding a second one.
- Where the provider does not report it, a conservative default the UI NAMES as a default. A
  number the product shows must never be more confident than its source.
- A pre-flight estimate of the assembled prompt exists, computed before the call, because the
  decision it feeds must be made before the call. Characters-based and honest about it.
- The percentage is shown in the product and says it is an estimate. Asserted on the surface,
  not only in a unit.
- Provider-reported usage is DELIBERATELY OUT (deferred by the owner) — do not build it, and
  leave the seam where it will replace the estimate.

title: Download from the Files tree, browser half: the button the owner has asked for three times
description:
Owner has asked three times. The download backend and wire landed in nocx-9le.8.1; nothing reaches it. This is the browser half, which needs no further backend: the method exists and a browser saves a Blob itself.

WHERE THE ITEM APPEARS, by the same rule already settled for upload — it is about whether the person can reach the bytes otherwise. Remote tab: always, desktop and browser. Local tab in a BROWSER: yes, the file is on the backend's machine and the browser cannot reach it any other way. Local tab on the DESKTOP: no — the file is already on that disk and Show in Finder is the action for it.

The desktop native save dialog is a second half and needs a method in internal/transport, which another worker holds; it follows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Download on a FILE row in the Files tree, on the machines named above, absent on the ones where it is not — tested in all four combinations.
- It goes through the operations surface: a download appears in the list with progress and cancel, the same row as an upload, because that surface was built for operations rather than uploads.
- The browser saves the file with its own name; the renderer never names a destination path.
- A failure is reported the way an upload's is, through the same seam.
close_reason: Merged as 8bb3d129 + the merge follow-up. Download from the Files tree, browser half: present on a remote tab in both builds and on a local tab in a browser, absent on a local tab on the desktop where Show in Finder is the action — tested in all four combinations, because the absences are the rule and an untested absence is not one. It shows in the operations list as the same row an upload uses. The row's destination field carries the SOURCE path, argued rather than fudged: a browser never tells the page where it saved the file, so showing a guessed ~/Downloads would be the renderer inventing an answer, while the source path is what lets a person tell two files of the same name apart. MERGE-ONLY DEFECT, resolved by the worker rather than by me: ops-row-detail added machine and startedAt to Operation while this branch was building a second adapter without them, so the merged tree did not compile — neither branch could see it. It took the shared derivation (machine-name.ts, one owner) rather than adding a parallel path. The desktop native save dialog is a separate half and still missing.

title: An operation row says nothing once it is done, and its numbers are unreadable while it runs
description:
Owner, running the product. A finished row reads 'appicon.png · Done · /home/dev' and carries no information at all: no size, no when, no how long. And while running, the byte counter and the speed change far faster than they can be read.

The speed and the readability are TWO problems, and fixing one leaves the other. The value jitters because speed is computed from consecutive samples over an uneven network; that wants smoothing. The display repaints far faster than an eye can fix on a number; that wants the RENDER throttled to a few times a second, independently of how often data arrives.

The trap: the last update must always land, or a throttled row freezes at 98 percent and never shows completion. Terminal states render immediately, bypassing the throttle.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A finished row carries size, when it happened, and how long it took.
- A running row's numbers are readable: smoothed value, render throttled to a few updates a second.
- The final update always lands and terminal states are immediate — tested, because this is the defect a throttle introduces.
- Time and duration are formatted by one owner, not by each caller; the kit already has format-bytes for the size half.
close_reason: Merged as 12208ec5. The row now carries size, when it landed and how long it took, worded by format-bytes/format-time — one owner, never assembled at the call site — with the exact moment on hover because the relative label ages. Speed is smoothed AND the render is throttled: two separate defects, and the trap the throttle creates is tested, so a row cannot freeze at 98 percent. WHICH MACHINE reads before the destination as one fact, and the worker hit a real boundary getting it there: the machine had to be recorded at flow.send, whose only two call sites were its own file and one locked to another worker. It stopped and asked rather than crossing or silently dropping half the task. My call was the composition root — the machine is a property of the BINDING, not of the gesture, so deriving it once where bindings are known beats two callers remembering a field and a third forgetting it.

title: Cancelling an upload reports that the server refused the body with a 500
description:
Owner, running the product. Pressing Cancel produces the row saying Cancelled AND a toast saying 'calmhub.zip: the server refused the body (500)'. Two messages about one event, contradicting each other, and the toast blames the server for something the person did on purpose. 500 also means internal error, which a deliberate cancellation is not.

Two halves in two layers. FRONTEND: upload-flow.ts:131 maps any non-409/410 status to 'the server refused the body'; when the renderer already knows the transfer was cancelled, a body-send failure must raise no error toast at all — cancelling is intent succeeding. BACKEND: the POST handler answers 500 when the transfer is cancelled under it; cancellation needs an answer that says so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a large upload, press Cancel.
2. The row reads Cancelled and a red toast reads: the server refused the body (500).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Cancelling raises no error toast.
- The backend does not answer 500 for a transfer cancelled on purpose; whatever it answers is distinguishable from a genuine internal error and the renderer maps it as such.
- A GENUINE body refusal still toasts — proven by test, so the fix is not 'stop reporting failures'.
close_reason: Merged as 26a4bb06. Cancelling raises no error toast — it is intent succeeding — while a genuine body refusal still does, with a test for each, so the fix is not 'stop reporting failures'. The backend half, which answers 500 for a deliberate cancellation, is still open.

title: The bell shows what you missed
description:
Spec: .internal/specs/2026-08-22-notification-centre-design.md (commit 81a13469)

Amends decisions #3 and #8 of the 2026-08-13 notification system design.

## What a user can do that they could not before

Open the bell in the activity bar and see what happened while they were not
looking -- including the events no banner showed them -- and mark them read.

## Scope

Ingress (stamps At/Level/Attribution once, mints OccurrenceID, fans out to feed
and policy); the bounded in-memory feed with eviction, byte budget and a visible
dropped-row; flood collapse keyed on (BackendID, SessionID, Kind, Level) inside
its own bounded window; notify.feed.read / feed.changed / feed.markRead with
contracts, generated types and both conformance tests; the activity-bar bell
with unread count and mark-read; click-to-tab resolved in the RENDERER (which
already owns session->tab), so this does not depend on nocx-jiwq.1.

Plus its own first honest source: session.ended. Without it the only raisable
event is program.notify, which the user started and is usually watching.

Router.Raise stops stamping At; ingress does. Policy stays in front of the
router, unchanged, behind ingress.

## Success Criteria

- With the window unfocused, a session on a remote host ends; the bell shows an
  unread row naming that session and its cause; clicking the row focuses the
  tab; the unread count returns to zero and the row remains in the feed.
  Watched end to end by one automated check driving the UI, not the store.
- A flood test raises N occurrences from one session and asserts BOTH that the
  feed stays inside MaxOccurrences and MaxRetainedBytes AND that a pre-existing
  unread danger row from another session is still present afterwards.
- deadcode -tags gtk3 -whylive on the feed's write path shows a path from main.

## Deliberately out

Persistence across restart; the 151 existing showToast sites (form feedback);
grouping beyond consecutive-run collapse (epic 2); per-channel settings (epic 3).
close_reason: All eleven children closed. The epic's DONE WHEN -- one automated check watching a user do the thing -- is e2e/notification-centre.spec.ts, green in the container and in CI's ci-e2e on both chromium and webkit at commit 08168b4f. CI run 32593712918 is green in every job: ci-mac, ci-linux in both keyring variants, ci-backend in both, ci-frontend, ci-e2e. Two reds on the first attempt were intermittent and are filed (nocx-lc15n, nocx-tm9wo), both in packages the epic does not touch, both green on rerun at the same commit. The reachability ratchet prints a path from main to notify.Feed.Add through monitorExit and Ingress.

title: Watch an imported path variable send without an environment
description:
The epic's DONE WHEN: a person imports a Postman collection whose request has
a path variable, opens that request and sends it, without touching an
environment at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Driven through the seam a person reaches: the import ask, the tree, Send.
- The check's own server asserts it received the resolved path — otherwise it
  passes on a request that carried `{{id}}` literally.
- Nothing waits on a duration.

title: The panel edits a request's variables and says which scope answered
description:
The request editor grows a Variables section beside Params, and the variable
panel learns the second scope: it says where a value came from — this request
or the environment — and offers to add the name at either.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The section lists the request's own rows and is editable like the query
  table; a row added there is written to the request's file on Save.
- The panel's header names the SCOPE of the value it is showing.
- The panel offers "add to this request" and "add to <environment>", and the
  one a person picks is where the row lands.
- A `:name` segment in the address is recognised and offered as a variable —
  never substituted silently, because our substitution grammar is `{{name}}`
  and pretending otherwise would be a second one.

title: The importer puts a path variable where it can live
description:
A Postman export puts a path variable's value beside the address —
`/users/:id` with `url.variable: id = 54321`. The importer reports the loss
today (nocx-6hg2w.16) because there was nowhere to put it. Now there is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `/users/:id` arrives as `/users/{{id}}` with `id = 54321` in the request's
  own variables.
- The rewrite is REPORTED in the same list the import already uses for what it
  changed — a person comparing with Postman must be able to see why the text
  differs.
- A `:name` segment with no value in the export still arrives rewritten, with
  an empty value in the table, so the address names something the panel can
  offer to fill.
- The scheme's colon and a port are not path variables and are not rewritten.
- A collection with no path variables is byte-for-byte what it is today.
close_reason: landed on feat/api-testing in 055e8991

title: The request's variables win, and the environment's are inherited
description:
Resolution order becomes: the REQUEST's own variables, then the environment's,
then the secret binding. `apicoll.Chain` already composes lookups in order and
`Snapshot` already builds one — this puts the request's lookup at the front.

The inheritance is the point and both directions must be tested: a name the
request answers wins over the environment's answer for the same name, and a
name it does not answer still resolves from the environment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Request wins over environment for the same name — asserted.
- A name only the environment answers still resolves — asserted.
- A secret variable is NOT resolvable at request scope: a request-scope row
  whose name the environment declares secret is refused by name, never
  silently shadowing the vault-held one. A credential in a request file is
  the thing this refusal exists to prevent.
- An unresolved name is still the `compose` failure it is today, naming the
  variable and the fields it was used in.

title: A request file carries variables of its own
description:
The request file gains `vars` — rows of name, value and enabled, exactly the
shape `query` and `headers` already have, so the model grows by one more list
of the same thing rather than by a new idea.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `apicoll.Request` carries the rows; the file round-trips them unchanged.
- `api.request.read` and `api.request.write` declare them in the schema, with
  the generated renderer type committed.
- A file written by an older build (no `vars`) reads as a request with none —
  greenfield or not, a missing list is [] and never a nil the renderer must
  check.
- A disabled row takes no part in resolution, exactly as a disabled query row
  takes none in the address.

title: A request has variables of its own, and inherits the environment's
description:
A variable can only live in an environment today, and an environment is the
wrong home for half of them. `id` in `/users/:id` belongs to the REQUEST: two
requests legitimately want different ones, and putting them in an environment
makes them collide. That is why a Postman export loses its path variables on
the way in — the importer now SAYS so (nocx-6hg2w.16) and still has nowhere to
put the value.

So the request gains variables of its own, and an environment's are
INHERITED: a name the request answers wins, and everything it does not answer
falls through to the environment exactly as it does now. One grammar for both
— `{{name}}` — because a second spelling for "a hole in the address" is two
owners of one concept, and what Postman gets right here is the SCOPE, not the
syntax.

`:id` typed by hand or pasted from documentation is recognised and OFFERED —
the mark says "make this a variable" — and never substituted silently. The
importer does the rewrite for a whole collection, `/users/:id` becomes
`/users/{{id}}` with the value in the request's own table, and says so in the
list of what it changed.

## Success Criteria

- A request can hold its own variables, written in its file beside its query
  and headers, and a person can add one from the panel.
- A name the request answers wins over the environment's; a name it does not
  answer still resolves from the environment — one test for each direction.
- The variable panel says WHERE a value came from, request or environment,
  and offers to add it at either scope.
- A Postman export with `url.variable` arrives with the value in the request's
  table and the address rewritten to `{{name}}`, reported as a change.
- One automated check watches a person import such a collection and send the
  request without touching an environment.

Deliberately out: a SECRET at request scope — a secret belongs to an
environment (nocx-ew3uv), and a per-request one would put a credential in a
file that goes into git.

title: Watch a token in the path go out and come back as a chip
description:
The epic's DONE WHEN: one automated check watches a person put a vault-held
token in the PATH — the Telegram shape, `/bot{{token}}/getMe` — send it, read
the answer, and see a chip where the token went.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Driven through the seam a person reaches: the environment editor to declare
  the secret and give it a value, the URL field to write the reference, Send,
  and the Raw tab to read what went out.
- The server the check talks to is its own and asserts it received the real
  value in the path — otherwise the test passes on a request that carried the
  literal `{{token}}`.
- The rendered run contains no byte of the value, asserted on the DOM.
- Nothing waits on a duration.

title: A secret in the URL refuses a cross-origin redirect
description:
The credential rule strips `Authorization`, the cookies and the endpoint's own
custom headers when a redirect crosses an origin, because a value in a header
can be a credential. A value in a PATH or a QUERY cannot be stripped: it is the
target itself. So the same rule, applied honestly, has to refuse the hop.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A redirect to a different origin is REFUSED, by name, when a secret was
  placed in the request URL — the run says so and carries the hop it would
  have taken.
- A same-origin redirect still follows with the value intact.
- A run with no secret in the URL is unaffected: the header rule alone still
  governs it.
- The refusal names the origin it would have gone to, and never the value.

title: A secret resolves wherever text is sent, and the sender is told where it landed
description:
`Substitute` resolves `{{name}}` in the URL, the query, the headers and the
body from the environment's plain values, and `Environment.Value` refuses a
secret name deliberately (§8: a collection in a pull request must not choose
what a reader's request sends). The vault-held value therefore reaches exactly
one field — `Auth.Var`, resolved later by the sender.

`Chain` exists for precisely this: a second lookup, behind the environment's,
that answers a secret name from the binding document. What it must also do is
tell the sender WHICH values it placed, so the raw text can chip them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `{{token}}` declared secret resolves in the URL, in a query value, in a
  header value and in a body — one test each; a substitution that works in
  three places out of four is the shape that ships.
- The values placed are handed to the sender as NamedSecrets, so
  `MarkRequest` finds them: the raw request carries a chip at every position
  the value landed.
- A secret that the binding store cannot answer is an unresolved variable, in
  the same `compose` failure a plain one gets, naming the variable.
- A sealed vault during resolution answers the canonical sealed error rather
  than a run (the boundary nocx-pgp9c.7 drew).
- The collection file is untouched: the resolved request is a projection
  (§6.4), asserted by reading the file after a send.

title: The panel can mint a secret variable, not only the importer
description:
Only the Postman importer can mint a secret variable today: it writes the value
through the binding store while the environment file keeps the name. From the
panel there is no door at all, so a person who did not import cannot have one.

The editor already draws a `secret` flag on a row; what is missing is the write
— an RPC that puts a VALUE in the vault under the binding this collection and
environment key, and never writes it into the file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A row in the environment editor can be made secret and given a value; saving
  writes the name into the file and the value into the vault.
- Reading the collection file back shows the name in `secretVars` and no value
  anywhere in it — asserted on the bytes.
- Changing a secret's value replaces the bound value and touches no file.
- Un-marking a row (secret → plain) refuses rather than silently moving a
  vault value into a file that goes into git; the person deletes and re-adds.
- A sealed vault refuses the write with the canonical sealed error, so the
  existing unlock seam raises the prompt (nocx-pgp9c.7 did this for send).

title: A secret can be used anywhere in a request, not only in auth
description:
A vault-held value can be used in exactly one place today: `Auth.Var`. The
substitution that fills the URL, the query, the headers and the body reads the
environment's PLAIN values and refuses a secret name by name —
`Environment.Value` returns `("", false)` for anything the file declares
secret, deliberately, so a collection arriving in a pull request cannot choose
what a reader's request sends.

That is the right rule and it is only half a feature. Telegram's API puts the
bot token in the PATH — `/bot<TOKEN>/sendMessage` — and so do a dozen others:
an S3 pre-signed URL, a webhook with its key in the query, an old-style API
that wants `?apikey=`. None of them can be sent from this product without
pasting the token into a file that goes into git.

The machinery is mostly built and pointed the right way. `Chain` exists to put
a second lookup behind the environment's. `apisend.Send` already takes the
values it placed (`used ...NamedSecret`), locates them in the composed text and
marks them, so the raw view shows a chip where a token went and the bytes are
never rendered. What is missing is the wiring between them, the door that mints
a secret variable from the panel, and one decision about redirects.

## Success Criteria

- A person can give an environment a secret variable and its value from the
  panel; the value goes to the vault and the collection file holds the NAME
  only — asserted by reading the file back.
- `{{token}}` resolves wherever text is sent — URL, query, headers, body — and
  the request goes out with the value in it.
- The Raw view shows a CHIP where the value landed, in the URL as in a header;
  no rendering of that run anywhere contains the bytes.
- A cross-origin redirect is refused when a secret was placed in the URL: the
  header rule strips a credential on a crossing, and a token in a path cannot
  be stripped.
- One automated check watches the Telegram shape end to end: a token in the
  path, a send, an answer, a chip.

Deliberately out: a secret that is not in an environment (a per-request one),
and any surface that displays a secret's value — the renderer never has it.

title: "Allow in this session" cannot take effect in the session it was answered in: the run's grant is pinned
acceptance_criteria:
After answering "allow in this session", the assistant stops asking about that effect class for the
rest of that session — including the rest of the run the answer was given in.

## What happens

The answer IS recorded (sessionPolicyStore.Set, keyed by the run's session), but the grant the
gate decides with was minted at ask time (runGrantFor, ws_agent.go: runGrant := h.grantFor(...))
and is carried in askRunContext for the run's whole life. resumeRun re-drives with rc.grant, so
the overlay written by the answer is not read until the person's NEXT ask. Every further tool
call in the same run asks again, which is exactly what the answer said to stop doing.

ADR-0028 decision "escalate" says approval resumes "as a new attempt with a NEW GRANT, never by
mutating a running one (ADR-0020 §5)". Re-minting on resume is what the ADR already asks for;
the immutability §5 protects is against mutating a grant mid-flight, not against re-resolving it
at the point a person changed the policy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Ask the assistant something that makes it call readScreen twice in one run.
2. Answer the first prompt with "Allow in this session".
3. The second call asks again.

Depends on nocx-igu4y: while the resume cannot match ANY approval, this is invisible behind it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test drives one run with two proposals of the same effect class, answers the first
  "in this session", and the second one is not asked about.
- The answer still dies with the session (the store's Drop stays on every teardown path).
- "Allow once" is unchanged: it covers its proposal and nothing after it.
close_reason: Fixed in a5af51d3: resumeRun mints the grant again through grantFor(sessionID), so the session overlay written by the answer is in force for the resumed attempt. Nothing running is mutated (ADR-0020 §5) — the resumed attempt is built from a new value, which is ADR-0028's own 'a new attempt with a new grant'. Covered at the engine (TestAsk_ASessionAnswerStopsTheNextProposalAsking) and over the wire (TestAgentApprove_SessionAnswerReachesTheRunThatAskedIt).

title: The unverified-TLS badge fires on runs where nothing was unverified
description:
The `unverified TLS` badge appears on every run whose environment has
verification off, whether or not anything was actually wrong with the
certificate. So it fires on `httpbin.org` — a public host with a perfectly
ordinary Amazon chain — and it fires on the self-signed development host, in
the same colour, saying the same thing. A warning that is on most of the time
is a warning nobody reads, and the one run where it MATTERS looks exactly like
the twenty where it did not.

What the badge should mean: **we accepted something that would otherwise have
been refused.** That is knowable. The handshake completed and the chain is in
hand; verifying it afterwards against the system roots and the host name is
the standard library's own verifier (`x509.Certificate.Verify`), not a second
implementation of one — and its answer is exactly the sentence a person wants
on the run: self-signed, expired, name mismatch, unknown authority.

So the run carries the ANSWER rather than the setting, and the badge renders
from it — with the reason, because "unverified" without "why" is the same
non-information one step along.

Verification being off is still worth saying when the chain would have passed:
it belongs in the connection block as a quiet line, not as a warning badge.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Give an environment `insecureTls` and point a request at any public HTTPS
   host with a valid certificate.
2. Send. The run wears `unverified TLS` exactly as it would for a self-signed
   host, and nothing distinguishes the two.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `api.request.send` carries what the check WOULD have said: whether it was
  skipped, whether the chain would have verified, and the reason when it
  would not.
- The badge appears only when verification was skipped AND the chain would
  have been refused, and it names why in one word or phrase.
- Verification skipped over a chain that would have passed says so in the
  connection block and wears no warning.
- A run with verification ON carries the same answer without a second
  verification pass — it already verified, and doing it twice would be the
  second implementation this avoids.
- A failure at the handshake still carries no chain (net/http hands the trace
  an empty state) and must not claim one.
