Preserve native target rules as the sole access-class authority; do not scan, copy, mount, or special-case applications. Linked implementation for PR 91.
acceptance_criteria: Sandboxed shells resolve eligible explicit host-HOME grants through their usual ~/ paths on Linux and macOS while native RO/RW enforcement remains authoritative; required homeProjections metadata is exposed end to end; source and packaged native smokes prove RO, RW, nested, and retarget-denial behavior; documentation and contracts are updated.

title: The block does not settle when a command is submitted: the running region and the frozen block are not the same box
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a pane and let it reach a prompt.
2. Type `seq 1 10` and press Enter.
3. Watch the block's header.

Expected: the header takes its place and output fills in below it — moving up
as a terminal scrolls, never back down.
Actual: it sits still while the command runs, then leaps ~150px up the pane at
the moment the command has already finished; other commands end with a visible
drop back down.

## Cause

Four separate owners of the pane's height were moving at once. Measured frame
by frame in the e2e container (chromium, 605px scroller, 20px cell):

1. **The composer left the layout.** `hide()` set `display:none` at submit, so
   the scroller grew 77px and the scrollback — which hangs from its bottom edge
   (`.scrollback-inner` has `margin-top:auto`) — moved by that much. Fixed by
   suspending the composer instead: same flex slot, `visibility:hidden`,
   `inert`. This REVERSES a deliberate decision; the history and why the trade
   flipped are written on `suspend()` in editor.ts.

2. **The live region was measured before the grid had the rows.** xterm parses
   asynchronously; the measure was scheduled from `session.onData` one line
   after `renderer.write()`, so its animation frame read the grid without the
   output. A command printing everything in one chunk has no next chunk to
   correct it: `seq 1 10` measured three rows live, froze eleven lines, and the
   header leapt 153px up. Fixed by measuring on `renderer.onWriteParsed`.

3. **The frozen row pitch was not the grid's.** `.term-line` was
   `min-height: 1.2em` = 16.8px against a 20px cell, so every frozen line was
   3.2px shorter than the live row it replaced — six lines dropped the block
   19px at freeze, thirty would drop it 96. This is the vertical twin of
   nocx-yy9g and is fixed the same way: the renderer's measured `cellHeight` is
   published as `--term-cell-height` and the line lays out on it. It was also a
   fidelity defect standing still — frozen text denser than the live text it is
   a photograph of.

4. **The body padding was on one side only.** `.cmd-output` has 2px/6px; the
   live region had none, so the box changed by 8px at every freeze. Both now
   read `--cmd-output-pad-*`, and the controller reads the value off the
   element rather than repeating the number in TypeScript.

## What is left

A command that holds the shell (`read x`) still falls back by exactly ONE grid
row at the freeze. That row is real: the frozen body ends at the render fence,
and the grid's cursor sits one row below it — the row the next prompt would
occupy. The live region cannot drop it without hiding the cursor of a program
waiting for input, and the block cannot keep it without swallowing the row the
next command's echo lands on (nocx-4yhi). Bounded and asserted at one row; a
better answer needs the fence and the cursor to stop disagreeing.
acceptance_criteria: Submitting a command moves the block header monotonically: it may rise as output arrives, and at the freeze it must not fall back by more than one grid row. An e2e assertion in command-editor.spec.ts measures the header against the scroller before Enter, while running and after the freeze, and reads the tolerance from --term-cell-height rather than a literal.
close_reason: Four owners of the pane height fixed: composer suspended instead of removed from layout; live region measured on onWriteParsed instead of on write; frozen row pitch published from the renderer as --term-cell-height (vertical twin of nocx-yy9g); body padding shared through --cmd-output-pad-*; and .nocx-chip reset so a <button> chip is the same box as a <span> one. Measured in the e2e container: 'true' freezes with no movement at all, 'seq 1 10' and a three-line printf move up once and never back. Residual one-row drop on a shell-side hold is nocx-i4h04.1. Commit b97d30b3.

title: workspaces.reorder can never succeed: two rules forbid the same id
description:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have at least two workspaces.
2. Open a workspace heading's menu and pick Move up or Move down.

Observed: a toast, 'Could not reorder the workspaces: Invalid params: ids must be a UUIDv7'. Every reorder failed, whichever way it was sent.

## What is wrong

Two requirements contradicted each other. The transport refuses any id that is not a UUIDv7 (§7: layout ids are durable and client-minted), while content.ReorderWorkspaces demanded a permutation of EVERY stored workspace — one of which is the reserved 'workspace:default'. A renderer that included it was refused by the transport; one that omitted it was refused by the store. The error named the half that was not the problem.

## The rule

The default workspace is not a member of the arrangement a user made: it renders no chrome at all (§4.2), no surface offers to move it, and it keeps position 0. The order is the user-made workspaces, written at 1..n. The answer still carries every row, because the renderer replaces its cache with it and a list without the default would drop the workspace every ungrouped tab belongs to.
acceptance_criteria: Move up / Move down on a workspace heading reorders it and raises no toast; a reorder naming the default workspace is refused with ErrNotAPermutation; the default stays at position 0 whatever order arrives; the answer contains every workspace including the default; a store test states each of those.
close_reason: Landed on feat/workspaces

title: Filter sandbox access inbox by application and keywords
description:
## Context
The Sandbox access Settings page lists denied filesystem attempts but cannot be narrowed when many applications and paths are present.

## Expected Behavior
Add an application filter and a keyword filter to Settings > Developer > Sandbox access. Filtering is client-side and must not mutate, dismiss, resolve, or hide backend events permanently.

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can restrict visible access events to one observed application.
- User can search visible events by keyword using documented, deterministic matching semantics.
- Filters compose and can be cleared without re-fetching or changing event state.
- Loading, empty-inbox, no-match, error, resolve, and live-refresh behavior remain correct.
- Focused frontend tests cover both filters and their composition.
close_reason: Closed

title: Fix sandbox access paths truncated to root
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start a sandboxed shell.
2. Access a denied file or directory outside the allowed roots.
3. Open Settings > Developer > Sandbox access.
4. Observe an event whose path is only / rather than the attempted target.

## Expected Behavior
The event records the complete attempted file or directory path.

## Actual Behavior
The access inbox can display only /, losing the target file or directory and making the proposed rule unusable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A denied event records the complete attempted file or directory path, not only /.
- Relative openat/openat2 paths resolve against the tracee cwd or dirfd.
- Absolute paths remain complete after canonicalization.
- Focused regression tests cover the reported root-only failure.
notes: Diagnosis 2026-08-18: the observed `/` is not string truncation. A local strace of OpenCode 1.18.18 shows Bun component walking with `openat(AT_FDCWD, "/", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC|O_DIRECTORY)`, then `/home/`, `/home/<user>/`, and relative `package.json`. Under Landlock the first root directory open is denied, so later target syscalls never occur and the backend cannot honestly report a target it never observed. The inbox also intentionally observes only denied openat/openat2; metadata probes use newfstatat/statx/access and are not Landlock denial events. Blocked on product/security choice: explain strict root ancestor denials, or design a larger virtual/mount-root compatibility layer. Granting `/` read access is unsafe.
close_reason: Not a path truncation: '/' is OpenCode/Bun's exact first ancestor-directory open, and Landlock denies it before later target syscalls exist. Verified the generic RO chain and native enforcement; no OpenCode-specific change requested.

Brainstorming: workspace + tab-strip UX rework (the chip feels wrong in use)
description:
The workspace chip in the horizontal strip (nocx-isoph.5, workspaces UX design §4.3) reads as awkward in real use. The owner raised it while testing feat/workspaces and offered Warp's tab sidebar and Tabby's tab strip as references. This bead is the audit trail of the design conversation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Whatever it changes about §4.3 is recorded as an amendment, not silently diverged.

title: Add sandbox denied-access inbox
description:
## Context
Sandboxed commands currently fail without exposing which descendant attempted the denied filesystem access or allowing a deliberate future-session grant.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Linux and macOS observers record bounded, per-session denied read/write attempts without parsing PTY output or weakening native enforcement.
- Settings has a separate Sandbox access page showing attribution, path, access, count, health, and explicit Dismiss/Add global RO/Add global RW actions.
- Resolution uses backend-minted event IDs, revalidates the exact existing directory, atomically updates current global settings, and affects future sandbox sessions only.
- Events are memory-only PrivateMetadata; unsolicited notifications and ordinary logs carry no paths.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sandbox denied-access inbox and global grants
description: Extend the opt-in per-tab filesystem sandbox with a Settings surface for denied filesystem attempts. The backend must attribute each observable denial to the sandbox session and executable, classify the requested access, retain a bounded private-metadata event list, and never weaken native enforcement. The user can promote the denied directory into the existing global read-only or read-write baseline, or dismiss it; running policies remain immutable, so grants apply only to future sandbox tabs. Research and document deployable macOS Seatbelt and Linux Landlock observation paths before implementation; do not claim support where the OS cannot deliver events without extra privilege.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sandboxed shell on each platform for which nocx reports denial monitoring available, when a descendant is denied filesystem access, then a separate Sandbox Access Settings page shows a bounded event containing session/shell identity, executable, access class, and canonical path without PTY-byte sniffing. Each event offers Add read-only, Add read-write, and Dismiss; add actions atomically update the existing global sandbox path settings through backend authority, deduplicate entries, reject conflicts, and state that the grant applies to future tabs only. Unsupported platform/kernel/permission states are explicit and never fabricate or infer denials. Contracts, architecture/ADR, focused backend/frontend tests, native smokes, and security review cover the shipped behavior.

title: Sandbox action launches opencode instead of the specified interactive shell
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
1. Enable sandbox.enabled.
2. Invoke the sandbox action and select a workspace.
3. Complete the permission dialog.
4. Observe that authenticated bootstrap replaces the shell with opencode.

## Expected
The original nocx-y46q contract holds: Quick Connect exposes `Sandboxed shell…` with stable id `__sandboxed_local__`; after authenticated nocxify bootstrap the selected workspace contains an interactive sandboxed shell.

## Actual
nocx-y46q.17 reversed the parent contract and commit 11498f1e renamed the action to `Sandboxed opencode…`, added a fixed backend OpenCode intent, and executes `opencode` after bootstrap. Each ephemeral HOME also repeats OpenCode first-run behavior.

## Root Cause
A real bootstrap-artifact accessibility bug was conflated with an unrequested product change. The runtime-tree artifact fix is required; the fixed OpenCode launch contradicts the parent epic, its original spec, and nocx-y46q.5.
acceptance_criteria: The sandbox action is `Sandboxed shell…` with stable id `__sandboxed_local__`; its open request remains command-free; the backend does not resolve, authorize, or execute opencode; the enhanced bash/zsh bootstrap artifact remains inside the sandbox runtime tree and authenticates nocxify; after authentication the interactive shell remains foreground in the canonical workspace; ordinary local/SSH behavior is unchanged; OpenCode-specific status/transport/UI code and tests are removed; affected docs explicitly supersede the mistaken fixed-OpenCode decision; Linux sandbox PTY smoke and targeted frontend/backend tests pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: The renderer never tells open which pane it is opening, so every block's anchor is null in the product
description:
FOUND while closing nocx-rtg0.28, which put entries.pane_id in and derived it
from the session. The backend half is complete: open takes paneId, validates
its shape, resolves pane -> tab -> workspace, records it on the session, and
every ledger entry that session writes carries it. Verified over the socket.

THE PRODUCT NEVER SENDS IT. frontend/src/ipc.ts has three openers -
openSession, openSSHSession, openSSHSessionByHost - and not one puts paneId in
the params, though the renderer has held the id all along: PaneManager.mintPane
returns the UUIDv7 and hands it to TerminalContent as `paneId`, which already
carries it on history.record and secrets.paneClosed. So params.PaneID is empty
on every open in the shipped product, the session is the pipe of no pane, and
every block's anchor is null - the durable edge exists in the schema and no
user ever gets one.

THE SAME SEAM'S OTHER HALF IS ALSO UNWIRED. `grep -rn workspaceId frontend/src`
finds no reader for the open ack's derived workspaceId either. nocx-isoph.2
resolves it correctly and answers nobody; the workspace feature works through
the layout methods instead, so nothing went visibly wrong.

AND IT CANNOT SIMPLY BE ADDED, which is why this is its own bead rather than a
line in rtg0.28. mintPane calls this.layout.openTab(...) and returns
opened.paneId WITHOUT awaiting opened.created, so the pane row is written
concurrently with the session open. open refuses a paneId naming no pane -
deliberately, "the pane you named does not exist and you named no pane are
different facts" - so sending it today makes opening a tab a race whose loss is
a tab that never appears. The ordering is a decision, not an oversight to
patch.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. grep -n "'open'" frontend/src/ipc.ts - three call sites, no paneId.
2. Open a tab in the product, run a command, read entries.pane_id: NULL.
3. grep -rn workspaceId frontend/src - nothing reads the ack's field.
acceptance_criteria:
- Opening a tab sends the pane's UUIDv7 as open's paneId, and a test watches a
  command recorded in that tab come back anchored on that pane through the
  REAL wire — not through a store-level Submit.
- The open ack's workspaceId has a reader. It is derived (nocx-isoph.2) and
  today nothing in frontend/src reads it, so the derivation answers nobody.
- The RACE is closed, and named in a comment: mintPane fires layout.openTab
  and returns the id without awaiting `created`, while open refuses a paneId
  that names no pane. Either the open waits for the row or the backend admits
  a pane it has not seen yet — decided deliberately, not by whichever promise
  wins.
- With no layout store the id is still minted and open still succeeds: that
  path must not become a refusal.
close_reason:
Commit aab52603. Five of six criteria met outright; the sixth is met as far as
the spec permits and is recorded honestly below.

The renderer now names its pane on all three openers, and the race is closed
the way it was decided: mintPane returns PaneIdentity{paneId, registered} and
the session waits for its pane's row, so `open` keeps refusing a pane it cannot
resolve (nocx-isoph.2's decision, which stands). The readiness comes off the
SAME two-armed handler that already knew the answer, so the single-handler
structure and the unhandled-rejection comment it carries survive intact. Every
call site is covered, including the restore path (Promise.resolve(true) for a
row that already exists) and workspace creation, which needed a paneRef to
order the chrome against its own readiness.

Two things the worker did better than the brief. The identity REPLACED the bare
string in TerminalContent's constructor instead of arriving as an optional
extra — an optional type-checks when forgotten, and the compiler named all six
construction sites. And criterion 5 could not be met as written: a refused
create disposes the chrome BEFORE the session is requested, so there is no
second open to count. The first draft failed on toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2) and
was rewritten to assert the invariant over every call — no open names a pane
the chain does not hold — which is the rule rather than the dispose race.

+14 tests, 0 regressions (3225 → 3239 full frontend), tsc clean on both configs.
Coordinator verified the one thing the worker could not: the new await adds no
hang class, because a dead socket rejects pending calls (Dispatcher.
rejectAllPending), so `registered` resolves false and the open goes out
unanchored.

CRITERION 6, precisely: the ack's workspaceId is decoded onto SessionHandle and
read into the session-opened log. That is a decode-and-observe reader, not a
behavioural one, and there is no honest behavioural consumer available — the
contract says the field carries no behaviour and design §5.5 forbids any
surface before the fence epic from acting on membership. Inventing a consumer
would have violated the spec the field came from. What will consume it is named
on nocx-isoph.

Focused tests and browser smoke cover visibility and activation.
